Welcome and greet patients to the clinic with a friendly and professional demeanor. Register patients efficiently, ensuring completion of all required forms with accurate information. Handle insurance and billing inquiries, providing clear and concise information to patients. Aid ill or distraught patients as necessary and with available resources.

• Payment Collection: Collect payments, insurance co-pays, and prescription charges following clinic financial policies. Proactively and confidently request a card on file, follow-up on patient balances, and ensure timely patient payments.

• Clinic Coordination & Collaboration: Collaborate with the healthcare team to ensure seamless patient flow and efficient clinic operations, contributing to a positive and organized environment. Manage patient reservations (online and walk-in) and registration, optimizing patient satisfaction and provider schedules. Assist in scheduling specialist referrals as needed for patient follow-up. Work with attention to detail in all tasks, navigating between multiple software systems to follow protocols established by our occupational health partners in support of our Employer Services team.

• Front Desk Management: Answer and direct phone calls in a professional and timely manner. Keep the reception area organized and tidy, creating a welcoming environment for patients. Perform various administrative duties, including photocopying, filing, and maintaining daily activity logs.

• CMD Technology & Offerings Expert: Become familiar with scope of services provided at CMD and costs affiliated with all services. Navigate and utilize various software systems for reservation scheduling and electronic medical records.

Required Availability

• Must be able to work 12-hour shifts in consecutive and or non-consecutive days: For full-time: Must be able to work three (3) 12-hour shifts a week with at least four (4) shifts a month on a Saturday or Sunday. For part-time: Must be able to work two (2) 12-hour shifts per week with at least two (2) shifts a month on a Saturday or Sunday. For per diem: Must be able to work four (4) 12-hour shifts per month, ideally working one (1) shift each week.

• Flexibility to work nights, weekends, holidays.

• When needed, must be able to work at a minimum of three (3) other ConvenientMD locations within a one (1) hour travel distance from your primary clinic.

• Required to travel for training shifts which will occur outside of your primary clinic within a one (1) hour commute.

Who You Are

• Education: High School Diploma or GED required.

• Proactive and confident communicator (written and verbal): Foreshadows and elevates concerns as they arise, unafraid of professional directness both with colleagues and patients.

• Detail-oriented with excellent organizational skills: Ability to juggle and prioritize multiple high-priority tasks and handle a fast-paced work environment.

• Compassionate, authentic, and patient focused: Supports patients through kindness; demonstrating understanding for others and contributing to the creating a community of belonging.

• Technically savvy: Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite or related software.

• Effective communicator and cross collaborator: Ability to establish and maintain positive relationships with patients, team members, and stakeholders across the organization.

• Excellent team player: You enjoy collaborating with others and being a part of a strong team dynamic.

• Driven and self-motivated: Capable of working independently, possess a level of initiative and enthusiasm to help drive results. Actively identifying better ways of working. Uses resourced to achieve the best outcomes for patients, the team, and the organization.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills: Able to comprehend, interpret, and apply the appropriate sections of applicable laws, guidelines, regulations, ordinances, and policies.

• Trustworthy: Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle all patient information in accordance with HIPAA regulations.

Bonus Qualifications

• Medical Receptionist certification

• Previous experience in a medical receptionist role or similar customer service position

• Familiarity with medical terminology and basic knowledge of insurance processes

• Experience using electronic records management software and other related programs used for medical registration and collection of HIPAA documentation

• Experience working with insurance billing and coding information

Pay Transparency

In order to maintain equity among team members, ConvenientMD has established defined hourly pay ranges for each role. Individual pay is determined based on a variety of factors, including but not limited to location, years of relevant experience, current market conditions, and budget considerations. The pay range listed reflects the potential compensation for this role within this region. Final compensation is determined at the conclusion of the interview process. If your desired compensation falls within the listed range, we encourage you to apply and learn more.

Hourly Pay Range for this Position

$20—$25 USD

Why You'll Love Working With Us

• Collaborative team environment that encourages professional growth

• Urgent care services at no cost to our team members and their families

• Extensive benefit offerings including health, dental, and vision coverage, company paid short-term disability, and optional pet insurance

• 401k match after one year of service

• Access to our primary care (depending on location)

• Educational Alliance with Purdue University Global and reduced tuition rates for team members and their families

• Employer rewards and access to discounts offered on services and products such as hotels, travel, entertainment, restaurants, and more

There's a job and then there's purposeful, transformative work. Our aim is to create a workplace where you can learn, grow, and continuously refine your skills. Applicants rarely meet every single job requirement, and we appreciate that many skills and backgrounds can make people successful in this role. We are committed to creating a strong sense of belonging for all team members, and our process is designed to prevent discrimination against applicants regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, age, disability status, or any other aspect which makes you unique. If you’re looking for a great next step, and want to feel good about what you do, we’d love to hear from you.

This role exists to define how CoLab wins and grows inside the PLM ecosystems our customers already run, turning Windchill, Teamcenter, and 3DEXPERIENCE environments into a path to enterprise adoption rather than a reason to stall.

Every enterprise engineering organization we work with has a PLM strategy, a team that owns it, and a long list of programs competing for its attention. Design decisions get made in reviews and typically land in PLM, and the gap between the two is where context gets lost, changes get re-litigated, and engineering teams lose hours every week. You will define how CoLab works with PLM, earn the trust of the IT and digital engineering leaders who own those systems, and turn PLM alignment into a repeatable advantage across the revenue org.

This is a deal-facing, customer-facing, and product-influencing role. The right person is part strategist, part operator, part competitor. Someone who can read a room of executives, build a hyper compelling value case on the fly, speak credibly to the PLM owner and the VP of Engineering in the same meeting, and close out the next step before the meeting ends.

Responsibilities

• Define and own CoLab’s PLM strategy, including how we position alongside Windchill, Teamcenter, 3DEXPERIENCE, and the rest of the engineering stack, and how design review decisions flow into the digital thread our customers are building.

• Map the PLM landscape inside strategic accounts, identifying who owns the roadmap, where modernization or migration programs are underway, and where review, change, and release processes break down between engineering and the system of record.

• Build the value case for PLM and IT leaders, why CoLab strengthens their PLM investment rather than competing with it, grounded in change cycle time, ECO quality, data continuity, and adoption across engineering.

• Run executive, IT, and engineering workshops that expose workflow friction between design reviews and PLM processes and create the urgency needed to mobilize multi-stakeholder buying groups.

• Collaborate on deal strategy for strategic opportunities where PLM and IT sit in the buying group, partnering with account executives to coach champions, navigate architecture and security reviews, and build the executive narratives that move buying groups forward.

• Shape CoLab’s relationships with PLM vendors and systems integrators, identifying where partnerships open doors, where they create a co-sell motion, and where they need to be managed carefully.

• Package PLM plays that account executives and customer engineers can run without you in the room, from discovery angles by platform to integration-led expansion sequences.

• Synthesize signals from strategic accounts into structured product feedback on integrations and the connected PLM experience, and validate product concepts with key customers so new capabilities fit how PLM-driven organizations actually work.

• Support the Director of Industry Strategy & Transformation with boots on the ground market trends, competitive dynamics, and customer insights across the PLM ecosystem.

Who You Are

• A mechanical engineer by background, with real-world experience in product development, engineering processes, and design collaboration.

• You’ve lived PLM from the inside. You have a deep understanding of the industry. You bring direct experience owning PLM strategy, implementation, or operations at a manufacturer, a PLM vendor, or a systems integrator, with hands-on depth in at least one of Windchill, Teamcenter, or 3DEXPERIENCE. You know how change management, BOM, and release processes actually run, and you can talk architecture with IT and workflow with engineering.

• You see the whole stack. You understand where PLM, CAD, ERP, MES, and point tools meet, where the digital thread breaks in practice, and how to position a new platform so it strengthens what a customer already owns.

• High emotional intelligence and the ability to read a room of executives in real time. You know when to push, when to pause, when to ask the harder question, and when to take the win and move on.

• Competitive by nature. You are wired to play to win, you put in the reps, and you run at high cadence. You take losses personally enough to learn from them but not personally enough to slow down.

• Strong context switching ability. You can move from a board level value conversation to a PLM architecture review to a workflow mapping session back to back and bring the right focus to each one.

• Sharp sense of time value. You understand which work compounds, which work is throwaway, and which conversations are worth a calendar hold versus a quick Slack. You make calls and you move.

• Strong commercial acumen and the ability to translate technical capability into business outcomes that resonate with VPs of Engineering, CIOs and PLM leaders, CEOs, and CFOs.

• Operationally wired. You understand how work actually gets done inside complex organizations. You can spot process drag, identify where reviews break down, and connect workflow-level friction to business-level cost. You don’t just diagnose, you translate it into a path forward.

• Clear, direct communicator. You write concisely, present without filler, and can build a clean, compelling deck under pressure. You know that a strong deck is a forcing function, not a deliverable, and you build them that way.

• Fluent with AI tools as a force multiplier. You know how to use AI to compress research, sharpen messaging, and build faster. You don’t just tolerate the tools, you intentionally reach for them to do more with less.

What Success Looks Like in Year One

• You have defined CoLab’s PLM strategy, and PLM and IT leaders at multiple strategic accounts are actively supporting CoLab as a result.

• You are owning PLM and transformation workshops with our top enterprise accounts.

• Your PLM plays are in use across the revenue team, with partner-sourced or integration-led pipeline you can point to.

• You have meaningfully influenced and supported the outcome of multiple seven figure deals.

• You are trusted to drive customer conversations without backup.

jobs.title: Director of SOC (Standard of Care) Operations and Revenue Cycle
jobs.description:

Status: Full-time, Salary, Exempt

Muon Space is seeking motivated and enthusiastic Electrical Hardware Engineers to join our growing team in San Jose, CA. You will work closely with experienced engineers across various disciplines to bring innovative satellite systems to life.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

• Schematic capture and PCB layout

• Bring-up, testing, and validation of newly designed hardware.

• Collaborate with software engineers on the integration and testing of hardware and software components.

• Build and test early hardware prototypes to evaluate design concepts and mitigate risks.

• Work cross-functionally with mechanical, software, systems, and production teams to ensure successful integration and manufacturability of hardware.

• Contribute to the creation of design documentation, test procedures, and reports.

• Participate in design reviews and provide constructive feedback.

• Mentor other engineers and push the team to new heights in your respective domain

• Experience in hardware engineering, preferably with exposure to electronic systems (relevant internships and academic projects will be considered).

• Familiarity with electronic components, circuits, and test equipment (e.g., oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies).

• Expert level knowledge in schematic capture and PCB layout software (e.g., Altium, Cadence/Orcad).

• Understanding of microcontrollers and common communication interfaces (e.g., UART, SPI, I2C, CAN, Ethernet).

• Experience with embedded systems, embedded programming concepts and comfortable in a Linux development environment

• Strong problem-solving skills and a hands-on approach to engineering challenges.

• Excellent communication and teamwork skills.

• A strong desire to learn and contribute in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.

Nice-to-have Skills

• Exposure to scripting languages like Python for test automation or data analysis.

• Experience with power electronics for space applications (e.g., batteries, GaN switching converters, load switch design)

• Experience with FPGAs, SoC, or embedded linux platforms

• Leadership experience in clubs or on small teams

jobs.title: Industry Strategy Lead, Systems
jobs.description:
About CoLab

At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.

CoLab is the AI platform for driving stronger engineering decisions. Every design review in CoLab builds a knowledge repository of design feedback, decisions, and lessons learned - which AI agents draw from to flag issues on future designs before they compound. The more your team works in CoLab, the smarter it gets and the faster you arrive at the ideal design. Companies like Ford, Komatsu, and Johnson Controls use CoLab to catch issues earlier, eliminate rework cycles, and bring products to market faster.

Founded in St. John’s, Newfoundland, CoLab has grown quickly from our first customer in 2019 to a rapidly scaling company. We’ve recently been recognized on Deloitte’s Fast 50™ and Fast 500™, and named a Canadian company to watch by The Globe and Mail and Financial Post.

Role Summary

This role is a high-leverage operator reporting into the Director of Industry Strategy & Transformation, with direct exposure to revenue leadership and account owners. This role exists to define how CoLab wins with systems engineering organizations, connecting design review decisions to the requirements, interfaces, and verification work systems engineers own, and positioning CoLab as part of how complex products get engineered end to end.

Complex products fail at the boundaries. Requirements drift as designs mature, interfaces between mechanical, electrical, and software teams get negotiated in hallway conversations, and integration and test surface issues that a design review should have caught months earlier. Systems engineering exists to manage that complexity. You will define how CoLab plugs into it, earn the trust of chief engineers and digital engineering leaders, and turn that alignment into a repeatable path for expansion across programs and disciplines.

This is a deal-facing, customer-facing, and product-influencing role. The right person is part strategist, part operator, part competitor. Someone who can read a room of executives, build a hyper compelling value case on the fly, talk requirements traceability with a chief engineer and program risk with a CFO in the same afternoon, and close out the next step before the meeting ends.

Responsibilities

• Define and own CoLab’s systems engineering strategy, including how design review decisions connect to requirements, interface management, and verification, and how CoLab fits alongside MBSE and requirements tools like Cameo, DOORS, and Jama.

• Run workshops with chief engineers, systems engineering managers, and design teams that map who owns requirements and interfaces, where cross-discipline reviews break down, and where issues escape into integration and test, creating the urgency needed to mobilize multi-stakeholder buying groups.

• Build the value case for systems and digital engineering leaders, grounded in requirements traceability, interface issues caught earlier, fewer late-stage design changes, and reduced integration and test risk.

• Co-own deal strategy on strategic opportunities where systems engineering sits in the buying group, partnering with account executives to coach champions, orchestrate alignment across engineering disciplines, program leadership, and IT, and build the executive narratives that move buying groups forward.

• Package systems engineering plays that account executives and customer engineers can run without you in the room, from discovery angles by SE maturity to expansion from one program to cross-program adoption.

• Synthesize and share signals from strategic accounts into structured product feedback on requirements, MBSE integrations, and cross-discipline collaboration, validate product concepts with key customers, and support the Director of Industry Strategy & Transformation with market trends, competitive dynamics, and where digital engineering and MBSE adoption are heading.

Who You Are

• A mechanical engineer by background, with real-world experience in product development, engineering processes, and design collaboration.

• You’ve practiced systems engineering at a high level and have a deep understanding of the function. You bring direct experience as a systems engineer, chief engineer, or systems or digital engineering leader in complex product development, ideally in automotive, aerospace, defense, industrial equipment, or medical devices. You know requirements decomposition, interface control, trade studies, and V&V from the inside.

• You think in systems. You see how choices in one discipline ripple into others, and you can spot where a program’s real risk lives before anyone else in the room.

• High emotional intelligence and the ability to read a room of executives in real time. You know when to push, when to pause, when to ask the harder question, and when to take the win and move on.

• Competitive by nature. You are wired to play to win, you put in the reps, and you run at high cadence. You take losses personally enough to learn from them and not personally enough to slow down.

• Strong context switching ability. You can move from a board level value conversation to a requirements walkthrough to a workflow mapping session back to back and bring the right focus to each one.

• Sharp sense of time value. You understand which work compounds, which work is throwaway, and which conversations are worth a calendar hold versus a quick Slack. You make calls and you move.

• Strong commercial acumen and the ability to translate technical capability into business outcomes that resonate with VPs of Engineering, chief engineers, CEOs, and CFOs.

• Operationally wired. You understand how work actually gets done inside complex organizations. You can spot process drag and connect workflow-level friction to business-level cost. You don’t just diagnose, you translate it into a path forward.

• Clear, direct communicator. You write concisely, present without filler, and can build a clean, compelling deck under pressure. You know that a strong deck is a forcing function, not a deliverable, and you build them that way.

• Fluent with AI tools as a force multiplier. You know how to use AI to compress research, sharpen messaging, and build faster. You don’t just tolerate the tools, you intentionally reach for them to do more with less.

What Success Looks Like in Year One

• You have defined CoLab’s systems engineering strategy, and systems and digital engineering leaders at multiple strategic accounts are sponsoring CoLab as a result.

• You are owning systems engineering workshops with our top enterprise accounts.

• Your systems engineering plays are in use across the revenue team, with cross-program expansion you can point to.

• You have meaningfully influenced the outcome of multiple seven figure deals.

• You are trusted to drive customer conversations without backup.

jobs.title: Enterprise Solution Engineer - South East
jobs.description:
Location: Remote – South East Region (must reside in FL, GA, SC, NC, or TN)

Sigma’s vision is to create an insight-driven world where people, organizations, and, ultimately, humanity are transformed for the better by data. At Sigma, we are building a cloud-native business intelligence platform that allows users to tap into their biggest databases hosted in the cloud and easily conduct ad hoc analysis to gain business insights in seconds. All without any SQL programming. We are growing the Solution Engineering team and are looking for a Solution Engineer who will help redefine the business intelligence landscape for our customers. You will join a talented team of Solution Engineers with a shared mission to truly make data access easy to drive business results.

The Sigma Solution Engineer believes in the power of analytics to transform organizations and uncover new data insights to increase business agility. The Sigma Solution Engineer will act as the trusted advisor to our prospects and customers working in tandem with Sales, Business Development, Product Management, Engineering, and Support. This individual is ultimately responsible for managing and delivering on all activities related to the technical presales cycle. This includes presentations, demonstrations, and hands on development of prototypes.  You will align closely with our field Regional Sales Managers (Enterprise)  focused on sales in new and existing accounts.

What You Will Be Doing

• Understand and uncover business challenges and issues faced by the customer and be able to run a targeted discovery sessions or workshop

• Engage with business users to define, create, and showcase solution prototypes

• Build and present customized demos for customers, trade shows, and webinars

• Confidently present and articulate the business value of the Sigma platform to all levels within an organization

• Deliver product, technical, and security related responses on RFPs/RFIs

• Participate in product, sales, and relevant technology certifications to acquire, maintain, and grow skill sets

• Work as a team player by contributing, learning, and sharing new knowledge

• Be conversant in integration and data migration approaches to facilitate enterprise-type sales cycles

• Manage multiple customer engagements concurrently

• Attain quarterly and annual objectives assigned by management

• Become a Sigma champion and product expert, prospects and customers will look to you for advice and expertise

Qualifications We Need

• Minimum 5 years of business intelligence experience

• Customer relationship skills

• Strong understanding of database concepts

• Cloud data warehouse experience - Snowflake, Redshift, BigQuery

• ETL experience - Fivetran, Matillion or traditional ETL

• Excellent organizational skills and ability to multitask in a fast-paced startup environment

• Experience implementing production business intelligence solutions or proof of concepts

• Bachelor’s degree in computer science or related field or equivalent technical & business experience

• 25% Travel

Qualifications We Want (also, skills you’ll learn!)

• Experience at a SaaS company or with cloud architectures

• Experience with data analytics business use cases

• Business consulting

• AI/Apps development experience

• Startup experience

About Sigma

Sigma is a modern analytics & business intelligence (BI) application built for the cloud. Trusted by data-first companies, Sigma provides live access to cloud data warehouses using an intuitive spreadsheet interface—empowering business experts to ask more of their data without writing a single line of code. With the full power of SQL, the cloud, and a familiar interface, business users have the freedom to analyze data in real time without limits. Sigma is self-service analytics as it was meant to be: a single source of truth that eliminates data extracts, simplifies analysis, and drives BI adoption at every level of business. Sigma is closing the gap between data teams and business experts. To learn more about Sigma, visit www.sigmacomputing.com or join the conversation on Twitter @SigmaComputing.

About us:

Sigma is the AI Apps and agentic analytics platform built on the cloud data warehouse. Business and technical teams use Sigma to explore live data, build intelligent applications, and automate critical workflows all without moving data or breaking governance. Sigma supports a spreadsheet interface, SQL, Python, and native AI in a single governed workspace, giving every team the speed to act and IT the control to scale. Sigma is trusted by more than 2,000 customers, including AMD, Duolingo, Colgate-Palmolive, and JPMorgan Chase.

Sigma announced its $80M in Series E financing in May 2026. The round was led by Princeville Capital, with new strategic investors Databricks Ventures, ServiceNow Ventures, and Workday Ventures participating alongside returning investors Altimeter Capital, Avenir Growth Capital, D1 Capital Partners, K5 Global, NewView Capital, Spark Capital, Sutter Hill Ventures, and XN. This milestone follows Sigma reaching $200M in annual recurring revenue in April 2026, with more than 100% year-over-year growth and 1.1 million new active users added in the latest fiscal year.

Come join us!

Benefits For Our Full-Time Employees:

• Equity

• Generous health benefits

• Flexible time off policy. Take the time off you need!

• Paid bonding time for all new parents

• Traditional and Roth 401k

• Commuter and FSA benefits

• Lunch Program

• Dog friendly office

Sigma is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a smart and strong team regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression, veteran, or any other protected status. We look forward to learning how your experience can enable all of us to grow.

Note: We have an in-office work environment in all our offices in SF, NYC, London and Sydney. All roles have a 25% travel expectation unless explicitly stated otherwise.

Our Privacy Practices

When you submit a job application on this site, Sigma processes your personal data for the purposes of evaluating your candidacy for employment at Sigma and as otherwise needed throughout the recruitment and hiring process. Please review Sigma’s Candidate Privacy Notice for more details. Please note that your personal data may be transferred to a country other than the one in which it was provided (including to the USA, the UK, and Canada, Australia).

Sigma’s use of AI

This hiring process utilizes artificial intelligence tools to assist in candidate screening and assessment. Our AI tools are designed to complement, not replace, human decision-making.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Senior Software Engineer

Minitab is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help develop and maintain our software products and systems. You’ll bring strong engineering judgment to complex technical challenges, help guide the design and delivery of meaningful product work, and support the growth of your teammates. This is an opportunity to make a lasting contribution to software used to turn data into decisions.

At Minitab, you'll do more than build software, you'll help transform the future of manufacturing. Every day, the world's leading manufacturers rely on Minitab to increase efficiency, improve quality, reduce waste, and make smarter, data-driven decisions that power better factories and better products. Our smart manufacturing platform connects data across the enterprise to uncover hidden capacity, eliminate bottlenecks, optimize machine performance, simulate improvements before implementation, and accelerate innovation through advanced analytics and experimental design. As part of our team, you'll collaborate with passionate, talented colleagues who are solving meaningful, real-world challenges for global industry leaders. With more than 250,000 users, 30,000 organizations, and 90% of the Fortune 100 trusting Minitab, you'll have the opportunity to make a measurable impact while growing your career in a collaborative, innovative, and customer-focused environment where your ideas matter.

What you’ll do

• Design, build, test, document, and deliver reliable software as part of a collaborative team, taking ownership of your work with a high degree of independence.

• Help maintain and improve product quality, security, scalability, and long-term maintainability.

• Strengthen automated testing, address technical debt, and find ways to improve the development experience for your team.

• Investigate complex defects, identify root causes, and help prevent regressions, including issues that cross systems or areas of code.

• Provide technical leadership in areas where you have expertise. Contribute to design discussions, share knowledge, and mentor junior teammates.

• Support production software, including participating in on-call rotations when needed, investigating incidents, resolving defects, and contributing to follow-up reviews.

• Plan and deliver medium to large features or projects with cross-functional partners. Break work into prioritized increments, communicate risks, and help keep delivery on track.

• Give thoughtful, timely code reviews and keep teammates and stakeholders aligned on objectives and priorities.

• Continue learning and help your team grow by sharing what you learn.

What you’ll bring

• At least 5 years of progressive experience developing commercial software.

• A bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• A strong understanding of software design principles, algorithms, and data structures.

• Proficiency in one or more programming languages, such as C++, C#, Python, or JavaScript.

• Proficiency with web development technologies, including HTML/CSS and JavaScript, and experience with frameworks such as React, Vue.js, .NET Core, or Node.js.

• Strong written and spoken English skills.

This is an onsite position at our State College, PA headquarters and candidates must be within commutable distance of State College, PA for consideration. Remote work is not an option for this position.

This position is ineligible for visa sponsorship.

To be considered for this role, you must be legally authorized to work in the United States and not require sponsorship for employment now or in the future.

Our Benefits:

HEALTH INSURANCE:  Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance is provided at no cost for full-time employees upon date of hire. Low co-pay pharmacy benefit and affordable family coverage plan is available. Short and Long Term Disability is fully paid by Minitab. Employee Assistance Program (EAP) - Provides guidance for personal issue and information on other Work Life Matters.

LIFE INSURANCE:  Group Term Life Insurance is provided at no cost for full-time employees at three times employee base salary. Minitab provides eligible employees the opportunity to purchase Voluntary Life Insurance for themselves and eligible dependents at affordable rates.

RETIREMENT PLANNING:  A 401k Retirement Plan with T. Rowe Price is provided with eligible employee contribution immediately. Minitab will match dollar for dollar up to the first 6% of employee’s contribution. Employees are fully vested in the Minitab, LLC 401(k) Retirement Plan upon date of hire.

PAID TIME OFF:  Paid holidays, as well as 4 weeks of annual paid time off are provided. The annual paid time off increases one week every five years.

HIGHER AND PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT:  The pursuit of ongoing development is important and valued at Minitab. In support of this value, Minitab offers tuition and related expenses assistance for both higher education and other professional development.

FLEXIBLE SPENDING ACCOUNT:  Medical and Dependent Care Reimbursement Accounts - Pre-tax Deductions. Parking and Transit - Pre-Tax Deductions.

HYBRID WORK SCHEDULE:  We offer a hybrid work model for eligible positions.

PREMIUM BENEFITS:  At our State College, PA Headquarters, there is an onsite gym, indoor swimming pool, yoga studio, movie theater, outdoor sand volleyball court, game room, arcade room and even a golf simulator. Personal training and nutrition counseling is available upon request.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

Job application remains open until filled.

jobs.title: IT Help Desk Analyst
jobs.description:
IT Help Desk Analyst

LaVergne, TN (hybrid, up to 3 days in office) | Full-time, Exempt | Up to 50% travel

About the Role

The IT Help Desk Analyst will work closely with our external clients to support desktops, network peripherals, various software applications, and server-related activities to support the growing demand for our products and services. This role will provide support services with technical problems involving desktop, laptop, or network services from local and remote customers.

What You'll Do

• Work closely with external clients, local and remote, to support desktops, laptops, network peripherals, software applications, and server-related activities

• Provide help desk support by phone and email across Active Directory, printers, hardware, software, networking, and Office 365

• Troubleshoot technology issues, determine the source, take appropriate action, and proactively follow up on tickets

• Handle service requests with a sense of urgency and a high level of customer service, keeping the help desk queue to a minimum

• Keep technical documentation and service requests accurate and up to date, including time spent and relevant details on tickets, for clear tracking, accountability, and communication with team members and clients

• Support, install, and train users on PCs and peripherals for pre- and post-implementation activities

• Take on project work as assigned

• Provide after-hours support as part of the On-Call team

What You Bring

• 1–3 years of experience troubleshooting application software, or related education/training

• Associate or Bachelor's degree in Information Technology preferred

• At least 1 year with Windows 10/11, hardware, and networking/IP configuration (DNS/DHCP)

• Working knowledge of Active Directory

• Hands-on experience with VPN configuration and troubleshooting

• Familiarity with IT ticketing systems

• Ability to explain technical issues clearly to non-technical users and clients

• Ability to work on-site in LaVergne at least 3 days a week

How you'll succeed here

• Analytical and Critical Thinking: Reviews and manages data with strong attention to detail; combines facts with likely possibilities; articulates and resolves complex problems

• Quality Focused: A recognition of the value of doing things the right way; has a high sense of integrity and thoughtfulness in your actions

• Clear Communication: Translates technical concepts into plain language for non-technical clients and users; listens to understand the issue before acting; keeps clients and teammates informed with timely, accurate updates.

• Achievement Orientation: results and commitment in the face of obstacles typical in a growth oriented, acquisitive software company; Motivated to achieve challenging goals; Exhibits a sense of urgency in solving problems and getting work done

• Self Confidence and Initiative: Exhibits confidence and approaches challenging tasks with a “can-do” attitude; Identifies what needs to be done and has a bias for action; Operates independently in absence of perfect information/direction

• Building Collaborative Relationships: Asks questions to identify shared interests; Digs to understand business concerns and perspectives of others; Consciously builds rapport and establishes common bonds; Builds trust with people whose assistance, cooperation and support may be helpful

Who you will be working for

Ever.Ag offers innovative AgTech solutions and services that empower agriculture, food, and beverage supply chains to feed a growing world. The breadth of the portfolio is uniquely capable of supporting the complex needs of companies involved in dairy, livestock, crops, and agribusiness. With decades of experience and industry-leading innovations, our technology, risk management, and market intelligence provide our customers with the tools and insights they need to operate more efficiently, sustainably, and strategically across every stage of the supply chain.

We welcome candidates from all backgrounds to contribute their unique perspectives to our team. Your success is our success!

Please visit our webpage to learn more about us News.Ever.Ag and https://www.ever.ag/

Please note, at this time, Ever.Ag does not hire candidates residing in Hawaii or Alaska.

Attention Search Firms / Third-Party Recruiters: Ever.Ag is not seeking assistance or accepting unsolicited resumes for this role. Resumes submitted without a valid written search agreement are the sole property of Ever.Ag; no fee will be paid if a candidate is hired.

jobs.title: Senior Associate, Partnership Channel Marketing (ABLE and 529)
jobs.description:
Vestwell is the financial technology company powering the new savings economy. The New York City-based fintech platform redefines how people save for the critical aspects of life across retirement, education, and healthcare savings needs. Today, Vestwell enables over 790,000 businesses and more than 2.75 million active savers, with over $57 billion in assets saved across all 50 United States.

Vestwell offers a range of products, including workplace-delivered retirement plans, employer-offered student loan repayment benefits, and various savings accounts for education, emergencies, and individuals with disabilities.

Vestwell's platform serves a diverse clientele, including financial advisers, employers, third-party administrators, financial institutions, payroll providers, government agencies, and individual savers. To learn more, visit vestwell.com

Who Are We Looking For?

Vestwell is seeking a proactive and strategic Senior Partnership Channel Marketing Associate to lead go-to-market strategy and execution for our ABLE and 529 state savings programs. You will work directly with state partners to plan launches, drive account openings and contributions, and sustain ongoing growth across saver, family, and advisor audiences. You will develop the GTM strategy, orchestrate cross-functional execution, and, when appropriate, manage external agencies to deliver scalable, compliant, and measurable marketing programs in a regulated environment.

You thrive in fast-paced settings, balance creativity with analytical rigor, and excel at relationship management with public-sector partners and internal stakeholders. You care about the people these programs serve, including individuals with disabilities and their families and families saving for education. You are a hands-on doer and a strategic thinker with exceptional project management skills.

What Will You Be Doing?

• Build and own the end-to-end GTM plan for new and existing ABLE and 529 programs, from pre-launch readiness through ongoing growth, including positioning, messaging, channel mix, timelines, and success metrics.

• Partner closely with state agencies and program administrators to develop compliant, co-branded campaigns and assets; manage review and approval workflows, accessibility requirements, and brand standards.

• Drive demand and engagement across the full funnel: awareness, consideration, account opening, funding and ongoing contributions, and retention. Design and execute lifecycle programs for savers, families, and advisors, including re-engagement of dormant or zero-balance accounts.

• Lead integrated campaigns across paid, owned, and earned channels, and tie them to key moments such as National ABLE Savings Day, tax season, and 529 Day. Coordinate with PR/Comms, events, content, and digital teams to maximize reach and consistency.

• Oversee external agencies as needed (creative, media, research); define scopes, timelines, deliverables, budgets, and performance targets; ensure on-time, on-budget execution.

• Enable partner and internal teams with toolkits and playbooks (GTM briefs, messaging frameworks, FAQs, decks, landing pages, email journeys, webinars, advisor and field collateral), including resources for financial advisors, benefits professionals, and disability and education community organizations.

• Establish KPIs and dashboards; track funnel health and program ROI (account opens, funded accounts, average balance, contribution rates); run performance reviews and QBRs with partners; implement test-and-learn optimizations.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Growth, Brand, Product, Data & Analytics, Legal, and Operations to ensure operational readiness and coordinated execution, including state conversions and platform migrations.

• Manage program calendars, workbacks, and risks; communicate status and results to executives and partners with clarity and consistency.

• Support forecasting and budget management for ABLE and 529 program marketing; monitor invoices, pacing, and efficiency metrics.

Requirements

The Necessities

• Minimum 2-3 years of experience in partner, product, or demand marketing, ideally in financial services/fintech or a regulated category; experience with public-sector or state programs is a strong plus.

• Demonstrated success building and executing GTM plans with external partners, including managing agency workstreams and complex approvals.

• Strong relationship-management skills with public-sector partners and senior internal stakeholders; confident presenter and trusted advisor.

• Proven project management excellence; skilled at prioritizing multiple concurrent programs and driving alignment across cross-functional teams.

• Data-driven mindset with hands-on experience setting KPIs, building dashboards, and optimizing campaigns; proficiency with analytics and A/B testing.

• Working knowledge of CRM and marketing automation (e.g., Salesforce, HubSpot) and collaboration/PM tools (e.g., Asana, Jira, Google Workspace).

• Comfort operating in a highly regulated environment; familiarity with accessibility standards and government brand/compliance reviews.

• Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills; crisp brief-writing and stakeholder updates.

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; advanced degree a plus.

The Extras

• Experience marketing ABLE, 529, retirement, HSA, or adjacent financial products.

• Familiarity with the disability community, special needs planning, or education savings audiences, and the advocacy organizations and advisors who serve them.

• Prior work with state agencies or public-sector communications.

• Experience building lifecycle programs for both B2B (advisor, employer, or partner) and B2C (saver) audiences.

• Multilingual abilities; Spanish a plus.

This role will be based in the New York City office, and will be part of Vestwell's hybrid in-office operation.

The expected base salary range for this position is $80K - $95K base. This position is eligible to participate in the Company Bonus Pool and is eligible to receive new hire equity in the Company. Please note that salary bands are based on NY and other similar metro areas and may differ based on where the role is ultimately hired.

Full-Time Employee Benefits
We’re an innovative, high-growth company with an exciting future ahead. At Vestwell, we prioritize employee wellbeing through comprehensive health benefits, generous time off, and a dedicated Employee Wellbeing Committee. Our hybrid work model offers flexibility while providing access to our collaborative offices in Midtown Manhattan, Austin, King of Prussia, and Scottsdale. And, of course, as a company focused on helping people save for the future, we offer a competitive 401(k) plan.

Interview Process
Our interview process starts the same for every candidate with 1-2 introductory conversations to learn more about your background, interests, and what you're looking for, while also giving you the opportunity to learn more about Vestwell and the team. From there, the process varies by role but typically includes a skills or experience-based assessment, such as a coding interview, portfolio review, or deeper discussion of your relevant experience. Successful candidates then move on to a virtual or in-person interview panel. Before extending an offer, we complete a reference check with a current or former manager and a peer. Throughout the process, we prioritize transparency, clear communication, and minimizing surprises.

For your awareness you will only receive correspondence from recruiting@vestwell.com any other domain not ending in vestwell.com is not our Recruitment team.

Vestwell’s Privacy Policy. Attention California residents: In the course of conducting our business and complying with federal, state, and local government regulations governing such matters as employment, tax, insurance, etc., we must collect Personal Information from you. Should you accept employment with Vestwell you may view our California Privacy Rights Act here: Vestwell’s California Privacy Rights Policy.

jobs.title: Project Manager, Event Transportation
jobs.description:
CharterUP is transforming the $365 billion global group transportation and mobility market with an AI native platform that powers modern charter, shuttle, and emerging autonomous vehicle operations. Trusted by many Fortune 500 companies, CharterUP connects enterprises, institutions, and event organizers with thousands of vehicles nationwide, while increasingly serving as the operating system for large scale shuttle and transit programs across airports, campuses, industrial sites, and major events.

Through real time availability, transparent pricing, intelligent routing, and AI driven dispatch and optimization, CharterUP replaces a fragmented and opaque industry with automation, accountability, and scale.

Why Join Us

• Innovative Impact: Be part of the team that's revolutionizing group travel, setting new standards in an industry overdue for change.

• Growth Opportunities: As a hyper growth company and one of the fastest-growing companies recognized by Inc., there’s no better time to join our dynamic, growth-stage organization.

• Driven Team: Collaborate with some of the most driven minds in tech, all while working in a remote-first environment with a tech hub in Austin, TX.

• Funding and Stability: Our $60 million Series A funding was just the start—we’re poised for even greater expansion, and you can be part of this exciting journey. CharterUp has achieved this growth profitability and efficiently, ensuring long-term stability.

Title:  Project Manager, Event Transportation

Reports to: Director, Enterprise Operations

Location: Salt Lake City, Utah (on-site at Project Locations, applicable within 2 hour flying distance of SLC)

About the Role:

CharterUP has been selected to deliver a landmark, multi-month visitor transportation program in Salt Lake City: a continuous park-and-ride shuttle operation running seven days a week from March through October 2027, moving thousands of guests from around the world between a dedicated park-and-ride facility and a high-profile downtown site.

CharterUP is seeking Project Managers to plan and coordinate the daily operation behind this program. Working with the Program General Manager, you will build and run the schedules, lead the On-Site Coordinator team across shifts, keep the transportation partner and client aligned, and make sure every day is planned, staffed, and reported accurately.

CharterUP is also hiring a Program General Manager and On-Site Coordinators for this program.

Key Responsibilities:

Plan and Coordinate Operations

• Build and maintain the operating schedule: shuttle frequency, vehicle assignments, shift schedules, and staffing coverage.

• Manage pre-launch workstreams and timelines, including site build-out, vehicle branding, equipment, systems, and staff onboarding.

• Track dependencies, risks, and open issues across the client, transportation partner, and internal teams, and drive them to closure.

• Plan ahead for peak days, special events, and schedule changes.

Lead On-Site Coordinators

• Schedule and supervise On-Site Coordinators across shifts, including handoffs, time off, rotations, and lodging logistics.

• Train coordinators on procedures, systems, and service standards, and check that standards are followed.

• Work on site during launch, peak periods, and disruptions.

Coordinate the Transportation Partner and Client

• Coordinate daily with the transportation partner on vehicles, drivers, dispatch, and maintenance.

• Work with client and volunteer leads on guest flow and staffing needs.

• Document client requests and service changes, and escalate anything outside scope to the Program General Manager.

Own Data, Reporting, and Documentation

• Ensure trip, ridership, and incident data is entered accurately and on time in CharterUP's systems.

• Produce daily and weekly reports for the Program General Manager and client; spot trends and recommend improvements.

• Maintain SOPs, checklists, and lessons learned for future programs.

Qualifications:

• Three or more years of project or program management experience in operations, events, logistics, transportation, emergency management, or the military.

• Experience building schedules and staffing plans for a multi-shift operation.

• Experience coordinating vendors or subcontractors and holding them to commitments.

• Experience supervising frontline staff.

• Highly organized, with strong follow-through on details and deadlines.

• Comfortable with data and reporting; proficient in Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, and spreadsheets.

• Clear, calm communicator under pressure.

• Ability to travel to Salt Lake City and work on site as needed, including weekends on rotation.

Preferred:

• Event transportation, shuttle, or large visitor-program experience.

• Military logistics or emergency management experience.

• Based in the Salt Lake City area or within a short flight.

What Success Looks Like:

• Schedules and staffing plans published on time, with every shift fully covered.

• Accurate, on-time data and reporting every day.

• Issues tracked and closed quickly across the client, partner, and team.

• A trained, reliable On-Site Coordinator team.

Salary

$1—$1 USD

Global Benefits & Perks at CharterUP

We believe great people can live anywhere—and they deserve great benefits, too. While offerings may vary slightly by location, we prioritize hiring near our hubs in Austin, Atlanta, and Miami as we grow our global team.

• Flexible Work Model: CharterUP operates as a remote-first company, with select roles requiring regular, in-office presence based on team and business needs. Role-specific expectations will be shared during the hiring process. U.S.-based employees may reside in any of our 19 approved states.

• Comprehensive Health & Wellness: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, mental health support, virtual care, gym discounts, and family-building benefits. In the U.S., we cover 100% of premiums for employees. International benefits align with local standards.

• Time Off to Recharge: Paid time off so you can truly unplug. U.S.: 15 PTO days (increasing to 20 after 2 years) + 8 paid holidays. International policies vary by country.

• Financial Peace of Mind: Company-paid life, short-term, and long-term disability insurance where available.

• Performance-Driven Culture: Join a fast-moving, ambitious, and collaborative team that wins together.

• Referral Rewards: Earn bonuses for bringing top talent to the team.

• Planning for the Future: Long-term financial planning support. U.S.: 401(k) plan. International: region-specific savings programs where applicable.

• Top-Tier Tech: Choose a Mac or PC, plus monitor, keyboard, and mouse to hit the ground running.

CharterUP is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive, accessible, and respectful workplace. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, ancestry, disability, medical condition, marital status, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws in the United States and Canada. If you require accommodation during the recruitment process, please let us know. CharterUP is committed to providing reasonable accommodations during the hiring process. If you need assistance or an accommodation, please contact your recruiter.

Hiring Locations: CharterUP U.S.-based candidates and employees must reside in one of the following states: Arizona, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Mississippi, Missouri, North Carolina, New Hampshire, Nevada, New York, Oklahoma, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Washington, and Wyoming.

We hire in the U.S. and Canada and are actively expanding our global footprint.

jobs.description:
At Morgan & Morgan, the work we do matters. For millions of Americans, we’re their last line of defense against insurance companies, large corporations or defective goods. From attorneys in all 50 states, to client support staff, creative marketing to operations teams, every member of our firm has a key role to play in the winning fight for consumer rights. Our over 6,000 employees are all united by one mission: For the People.

Social Security Disability Attorney

At Morgan & Morgan, we’re building one of the fastest-growing Social Security Disability practices in the country, and we’re looking for experienced attorneys NATIONWIDE who want to hit the ground running. You don’t need a decade of experience. But you do need drive, a sharp mind, and a genuine desire to fight for people who have nowhere else to turn.

Build a Practice. Change Lives. Get Rewarded for Winning.

Every day, people come to us after hearing one word too many: Denied.

Denied benefits they’ve earned.

Denied financial security.

Denied the support they need when they’re no longer able to work.

Your job is to change that.

At Morgan & Morgan, our Social Security Disability attorneys don’t spend their days chasing business or wondering where their next client will come. They spend their time doing what they became attorneys to do: advocate for people who need someone in their corner.

As one of the fastest-growing Social Security Disability practices in the country, we’re looking for attorneys who thrive in a fast-paced environment, enjoy managing an active caseload, and take pride in moving cases toward successful outcomes.

If you’re energized by staying busy, collaborating with a high-performing team, and being rewarded for your results, we’d like to meet you.

Why Join Us?

We’re not simply growing—we’re building one of the premier Social Security Disability practices in the country.

In 2024, our firm ranked in the Top 10 nationally among Social Security Disability firms by annual fees generated. We’re on track to become one of the very top Social Security Disability firms in the country. That growth creates opportunities for attorneys who want more than a steady paycheck.

Our compensation is designed to reward productivity and successful outcomes. In addition to a competitive base salary, attorneys participate in a bonus structure tied to resolved cases and annual fees, giving high performers the opportunity to significantly increase their overall earnings.

Just as importantly, you’ll inherit a robust caseload and consistent pipeline of clients, allowing you to focus on practicing law rather than generating business.

What You’ll Do

• Represent Social Security Disability clients through all stages of their claims

• Prepare clients for hearings and advocate on their behalf before Administrative Law Judges

• Manage a substantial caseload while maintaining exceptional client service

• Work closely with experienced case managers and support staff to efficiently move cases forward

• Develop legal strategy, prepare evidence, and build compelling cases for clients

• Help clients navigate one of the most important legal matters of their lives

Who Thrives Here

Our most successful attorneys tend to be people who:

• Enjoy staying busy and managing a high-volume practice

• Find satisfaction in resolving cases and seeing measurable results

• Like collaborating with experienced legal professionals in an office environment

• Are self-motivated and performance-driven

• Build strong relationships with clients during difficult moments in their lives

• Want their compensation to reflect their impact and productivity

This position is intentionally office-based because we believe our attorneys do their best work when collaborating with colleagues, mentoring one another, and working closely with their support teams. If you enjoy the energy of an engaged legal office and being surrounded by people who are all working toward the same mission, you’ll fit right in.

Qualifications

• JD from an ABA-accredited law school

• Active license and good standing with at least one US state bar

• Prior experience handling Social Security Disability hearings

• Existing Social Security Representative ID (preferred)

• Demonstrated ability to successfully manage a high-volume caseload

• Outstanding communication, advocacy, and client relationship skills

• Strong writing, organizational, and case management abilities

Locations

These positions can be based in any of our U.S. offices.

Our Mission

At Morgan & Morgan, the work we do matters. For millions of Americans, we’re their last line of defense against insurance companies, large corporations, and systems that don’t always work in their favor.

From attorneys across the country to client support, operations, and marketing, more than 6,000 team members are united by one mission:

For the People.

If you’re looking for a practice where your work has real impact, your calendar stays full, your colleagues have your back, and your compensation grows alongside your success, we’d love to hear from you.

#LI-JL1

Benefits

Morgan & Morgan is a leading personal injury law firm dedicated to protecting the people, not the powerful. This success starts with our staff.  For full-time employees, we offer an excellent benefits package including medical and dental insurance, 401(k) plan,  paid time off and paid holidays.

jobs.title: Registered Nurse, Eating Disorders
jobs.description:
Weekly outpatient therapy isn't always enough, and a trip to the ER isn't the only answer. Patients and their families rely on Compass Health Center when in crisis – every day, we help people overcome depression, anxiety, suicidality, obsessions/compulsions, trauma, chronic pain, and other obstacles in order for our patients to live freely.

About This Role

We are seeking a Registered Nurse to provide compassionate, direct patient care within our Eating Disorders Partial Hospitalization Program and Intensive Outpatient Program, supporting patients whose relationship with food, eating, movement, and body image is a primary focus of treatment. In this role, you will provide exemplary nursing care while remaining sensitive to the individual psychiatric, nutritional, and medical needs of each patient. You will work closely with Registered Dietitians, Primary Therapists, Group Therapists, Family Therapists, Psychiatry Providers, and other members of the interdisciplinary treatment team to support safe, coordinated, patient-centered care. This role will also include supporting the other non-Eating Disorders Programs across the lifespan (ages 5 and up) as indicated by census.

Our location in Northbrook is our first and largest facility, and consists not only of our widest variety of programs, but also serves as a pilot site for many of our new treatment offerings.

What You’ll Do

Medical Monitoring

• Complete nursing assessments and obtain relevant medical history

• Measure, monitor, and document vital signs and other clinical indicators

• Obtain and document patient weights in accordance with program protocols

• Monitor patients for signs of medical instability and promptly escalate concerns to providers and the interdisciplinary treatment team

• Monitor and communicate relevant laboratory results and other medical findings

• Collect specimens as ordered

• Support ongoing assessment of medical status in collaboration with Psychiatry Providers and Registered Dietitians

• Recognize how co-occurring OCD, trauma, anxiety, depression, and other psychiatric symptoms may present within eating-disorder treatment and communicate relevant observations to the treatment team

Medication Management

• Administer medications safely and accurately

• Assist Psychiatry Providers with prescription refills

• Coordinate with insurance companies regarding medication prior authorizations

• Monitor and communicate medication-related concerns, side effects, and patient responses

• Maintain compliance with medication storage, handling, and administration policies

Eating Disorder & Meal Support

• Provide direct nursing support during meals and snacks (as assigned)

• Support patients experiencing distress, anxiety, or other acute symptoms related to eating

• Collaborate with interdisciplinary treatment team regarding nutritional concerns, meal support, medical monitoring, and changes in patient status

• Assist with implementation of individualized treatment plans within scope of practice

• Support safe transitions between levels of care by communicating relevant medical and nursing information to the treatment team

Patient & Family Support

• Provide therapeutic, compassionate communication to patients and families

• Provide education regarding medications, medical monitoring, and nursing-related aspects of treatment

• Participate in interdisciplinary communication regarding patient progress, concerns, and treatment needs

Care Coordination & Documentation

• Maintain accurate and timely nursing documentation throughout treatment

• Assisting with the completion of medical documentation for patients and their families

• Assist Psychiatry Providers with laboratory orders and retrieval of results

• Participate in interdisciplinary rounds and communicate relevant medical observations

• Coordinate with outpatient providers of the patient's care team (as appropriate)

• Assist with medical and nursing components of discharge and aftercare planning

Phone Triage & Clinical Support

• Provide phone triage and respond appropriately to patient and family concerns

• Determine when concerns require follow-up, provider consultation, or urgent intervention

• Communicate changes in patient condition promptly to appropriate clinical staff

• Provide support and assistance during crisis or emergency situations

• Follow established protocols for escalation of medical or psychiatric concerns

Program Operations

• Perform basic materials-management functions, including ordering and stocking supplies

• Support medication inventory and program safety procedures

• Participate in required program training, supervision, consultation, and quality-improvement initiatives

• Provide support and assistance to organizational committees (as needed)

• Contribute to the development and continuous improvement of program standards and clinical workflows

• Participate in compliance monitoring and other program-quality initiatives

• Perform other duties as assigned

Who You Are

• Current Registered Nurse licensure in the State of Illinois (required)

• BSN (preferred); LPN candidates may be considered where appropriate

• Current Healthcare Provider CPR certification (required)

• Minimum of 1 year of hospital or clinical nursing experience (required)

• Experience in behavioral health or eating-disorder treatment (required)

• Experience in PHP, IOP, residential, inpatient, or other higher-acuity behavioral healthcare settings (preferred)

Skills & Approach

• Possesses excellent therapeutic communication skills

• Provides compassionate, nonjudgmental, patient-centered care

• Comfortable working in a behavioral-health environment and supporting patients experiencing significant emotional distress

• Comfortable monitoring medically vulnerable patients and escalating concerns promptly

• Able to recognize the interaction between psychiatric symptoms and medical/nutritional concerns

• Comfortable collaborating closely with Registered Dietitians, therapists, prescribers, and other clinical disciplines

• Demonstrates strong clinical judgment and attention to detail

• Maintains appropriate professional boundaries while building therapeutic relationships

• Practices with cultural humility and respect for individual patient experiences

• Values teamwork, continuous improvement, connection, innovation, and patient-centered care

• Able to work within established clinical protocols, program standards, and treatment-team recommendations

• Seeks supervision and consultation when appropriate

We are committed to a fair and equitable work environment. The expected compensation range for this role is below. This range includes multiple career path levels across the organization; where you fall in the range is dependent upon a number of factors including, but not limited to, your years of experience, type of experience, location, and education/certifications. Compass reserves the right to update these ranges.

Compensation

$31—$35 USD

We know job descriptions can be intimidating, so if this sounds like an opportunity for you, please don't hesitate to apply!

Who We Are

Compass Health Center is a recognized leader in crisis-level mental health, bringing passion, connection, and patient-centered care to the Partial Hospitalization and Intensive Outpatient space (PHP/IOP). Based in Chicagoland, we serve hundreds of patients every day, ranging from ages 5 through adulthood, in our onsite facilities or through our flourishing virtual programming. Compass fills a critical gap between outpatient and inpatient care through an intermediate level of Behavioral Healthcare.

A few more things we want you to know: our values are super important to us, and hopefully will be to you, too. Cultural humility, teamwork, continuous improvement, connection, patient centered care, passion, innovation, and agility should be your power sources. Joining Compass is an opportunity to feel fulfilled through a joint mission towards healing our communities.

Benefits & Perks

We know that you will be dedicated to your purpose here. We look at that investment as a two-way street. We are proud to offer plenty of space for growth, and opportunities to pursue continuous development within our organization.

For eligible positions, our other benefits include: comprehensive medical/dental/vision plans, 401k program with company matching, generous PTO (including competitive parental leave after 1 year of employment), and continuous training through CEU seminars and volunteering opportunities.

What’s Next?

Compass is committed to cultivating diverse and dynamic teams who exude passion for their craft, so whether or not you check all the boxes, we encourage you to apply – we’d be grateful to hear from you!

jobs.title: Auto Painter - Blue Mound, TX - 2nd shift - $4,000 Sign On Bonus
jobs.description:
We’re looking for Auto Painters with a minimum of 3 years of professional automotive painting experience to join us at Carvana - the fastest-growing used automotive retailer in U.S. history and one of the four fastest companies to make the Fortune 500.
As a Mid-Level Painter, you’ll be expected to match/mix paint color and use water-based paint to paint the vehicle inside our paint booths.

At Carvana, you’ll receive a competitive wage and amazing perks – including a 401(k) with Carvana match and even a vehicle purchase discount – all while using state of the art tools in one of our high-tech Inspection Centers (click here to learn more). If you’re joining us in an entry-level position, we offer training programs to make sure your skills and pay progress along with the company.

Other perks of the Job

• 100% company-paid healthcare premiums

• Generous paid-time off and your birthday is a holiday!

• ASE and tool reimbursement programs

• Tuition reimbursement and student loan repayment

Schedule:

We do everything we can to deliver an exceptional customer experience, and that includes delivering great vehicles when expected. If we're in a pinch, mandatory overtime is one way in which we can follow-through on this commitment to our customers. We're looking for team players who are all in on our mission and are able to work mandatory overtime based on our business needs.

How To Get Started
Join the Carvana team by applying on this page, or call one of our recruiters by phone at (888) 690-7853, Monday through Friday, between 6 AM and 4 PM PT (9AM to 7PM ET).

Not a match for this role?
We have a variety of paint roles available, depending on your experience - look below to see other roles available to help us get our low-mileage, late-model cars ready for our customers:

• Paint Prepper (min 6 months professional experience): prepare vehicles for cosmetic paintwork, including sanding, masking, taping, bagging, unbagging/tear down, and buffing

• Entry-Level Painter (min 1 year professional experience): prime vehicles and perform final sanding before the vehicle is painted, along with buffing, touch-up, paint mixing, and airbrush.

• Mid-Level Painter (min 3 years professional experience): match/mix paint color and use water-based paint to paint the vehicle inside our paint booths

• Experienced Painter (min 5 years professional experience): painting (base coats, tri-coats, solid, metallic, and clear coats), blending adjacent panels, and paint correcting vehicles.

We also have a variety of other automotive roles available in one of our 18 locations across the country – take a look at our Careers site to apply for one of the following roles:

• Auto Body roles: Paint, Prep/Body work, Wheel Repair, Airbrush, Interior Repair, Glass Repair, and PDR (Paintless Dent Repair) roles

• Auto Technician/Mechanic roles: Lube and Oil, Inspection, Brake and Tire, Mechanical Repair / Build, and Master Technician roles

• Entry-Level roles: Detailing, Inventory Associate (Car Porters), Photo, Parts Associate, Inspection, and Coordinator/Administrator roles

General qualifications and requirements

• Ability to physically operate vehicle equipment and tools - must be able to lift up to 60 pounds independently

• Must be at least 18 years of age and possess a valid driver’s license. Some positions may be subject to an Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check

• An ability to work in a fast-paced, ever-changing production environment while sometimes being exposed to excessive weather conditions (heat/cold)

• Use of safety equipment that may include but not limited to face shield or goggles, non-slip shoes, gloves, mask, and other protective garments and equipment

About Carvana

jobs.description:

You will work closely with application developers, security architects, and infrastructure teams to build secure-by-design integration patterns and accelerate adoption of zero trust principles across the enterprise.

We know that you can’t have great technology services without amazing people. At MetroStar, we are obsessed with our people and have led a two-decade legacy of building the best and brightest teams. Because we know our future relies on our deep understanding and relentless focus on our people, we live by our mission: A passion for our people. Value for our customers.

If you think you can see yourself delivering our mission and pursuing our goals with us, then check out the job description below!

What you’ll do:

• Design, develop, and maintain reusable frameworks, libraries, APIs, and reference implementations for zero trust authentication and authorization.

• Create developer guides, documentation, and best practices to enable smooth integration with security services.

• Strong, repeat experience with commercial or open-source identity and access management platforms (e.g., ForgeRock, Okta, Keycloak, Ping Identity).

• Strong expertise with fine-grained access control models (entitlements, row-level security, ABAC).

• Expert proficiency in at least one programming language (e.g., Java, Go, Python) for building frameworks and libraries.

• Solid experience with zero trust architecture and principles.

• Experience creating developer documentation and integration guides.

• Strong grasp of secure coding practices and software development lifecycle (SDLC) security.

• This position requires the ability to work onsite five (5) days per week. Candidates must be able to meet this onsite requirement for the duration of the role.

SALARY RANGE: $166,000 – $202,000
