You can expect to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, driven by first principles engineering, solving difficult problems.




JOB OVERVIEW 

The  Hardware Applications Engineer will own application-specific testing of Heron's solid state transformer (SST) across its core use cases: powering AI data centers, utility-scale BESS, and PV plants. That means bringing up hardware in the lab and at pilot sites, writing scripts to drive test equipment and power converters, and debugging performance against what each application demands, from MPPT performance and PPC/EMS/BMS communication to AI load smoothing and DC protection coordination. You will work hand in hand with the Systems Integration team: they own the SST platform; you own the applications.




HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE

 - Own end-to-end application testing of a novel high C-rate battery pack (SuperBBU) with Heron's SST, validating ripple mitigation, backup capability, slew rates, and power-loss profiles.

 - Support SST and utility-scale BESS integration testing at pilot sites, covering EMS-to-SST communication, black start and grid-forming coordination, charge/discharge cycling, and round-trip efficiency.

 - Support integration testing of the SST with commercial off-the-shelf DAS, SCADA and EMS systems. 

 - Own Heron's first pilot deployments: review field performance, identify feature gaps, and work with SW/FW teams to turn findings into product improvements.

 - Write and maintain Python-based test automation to command power converters, sequence tests, log data, and turn manual procedures into repeatable automated loops.

 - Safely operate power converters, chillers, contactors, and protection hardware, and set up cabling, instrumentation, and data acquisition for high-power test runs.




WHAT YOU WILL BRING

We have a short list of must-have requirements. We prioritize a strong grip on first principles, hands-on skills, and a sense of initiative. Domain-specific knowledge and experience will help determine the career level for each hire.




MUST-HAVE REQUIREMENTS

 - 5+ years of hands-on experience in power electronics, energy storage, EV, grid, or a comparable hardware-intensive environment.

 - Strong grasp on DC circuit fundamentals: resonances, parasitics, slew rates, and inductive spikes. You can correlate test data with simulation results.

 - Strong scripting and test-automation skills to drive instruments and power converters and to log and analyze data.

 - Working knowledge of power conversion and battery systems: inverters and converters, BMS, DC pre-charge, contactors and protection, and thermal and cooling loops.

 - Comfort with lab instrumentation (oscilloscopes, power analyzers, DAQ systems) and comms protocols such as CAN and Modbus TCP.

 - Scrappy mindset: you get things done with a hundred hurdles in front of you.




NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience with solid state transformers or grid-forming inverters.

 - Familiarity with utility-scale BESS commissioning, grid-support functions, or EMS integration.

 - Prior experience in systems-level testing of power electronics or energy storage products

 - Hands-on experience with circuit and system simulation tools such as LTspice, Simscape, or PLECS. 

If you are passionate about the energy transition and enjoy working at the frontier of power electronics and grid integration, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power.

Heron Power provides competitive compensation (salary and equity) and benefits. The base salary range for this role is from $140,000 to $200,000K.

jobs.title: Senior Fellow, Texas Climate Policy (Executive Branch) Contract
jobs.description:
Role: Senior Fellow, Texas Climate Policy (Executive Branch), 1-year contract with potential to hire in a full-time role
Role Purpose: To design and lead a year-long effort that puts Texas on the map for climate policy that cuts pollution while lowering bills.
Duration: 1-year contract starting early January 2027, with potential to extend or hire into a full-time role at the end of the term. Open to time commitment of between 20-40 hours per week. Project assignments will be adjusted to match capacity.
Location and Travel: Based in Texas; candidates outside Texas must relocate. In Austin at least 40% of the time (about 2+ days per week), with occasional out-of-state travel, including in-person team meetings.
Timeframe: Priority deadline for proposals is December 4, 2026. Target contract start date is early January 2027.
Compensation: We anticipate a maximum monthly rate of ~$15,500/month, depending on experience and demonstrated skill level. We expect total contract value to vary based on hours and scope.

About Climate Cabinet

Climate Cabinet helps state and local champions win on climate. We support high-impact, under-the-radar offices who have “outsized impact” on our ability to solve the climate crisis - from clean energy buildout to zero-carbon transportation. These leaders drive progress regardless of who is in the White House.

We are a dynamic, passionate team of experienced climate experts with staff on-the-ground across the country and a remote-first workplace. We create a clear, kind culture of agency and growth—sharing expectations openly, giving space for initiative, and supporting one another as full people to build their climate movement leadership in service of our climate mission.

Role Summary

Texas is the nation’s top emitter, and some of the fastest, most impactful climate progress in the state can come from the Governor’s office. Climate Cabinet is seeking a Senior Fellow, engaged as an independent contractor, to design and lead a year-long effort that puts Texas on the map for climate policy that cuts pollution while lowering bills. The work will be carried out mainly through executive action and the state executive branch engagement with major municipalities, rather than new state legislation.

The Senior Fellow will use Texas’s state budget, executive authority, and state-city partnerships to advance climate policy, and will help Climate Cabinet translate complex policy into advocacy, policy development, and public narrative. This is a high-autonomy engagement for an experienced policy expert, working closely with Climate Cabinet’s policy leadership and Texas team. Executive-branch work is a new area for Climate Cabinet, so lessons from this engagement will also shape our work in other states.

This is a 1-year fellowship, and we hope to transition the Senior Fellow into a permanent role. If that happens, the role’s scope, reporting, and duties may change substantially.

Scope of Work

The Senior Fellow leads Climate Cabinet’s executive-branch climate policy work in Texas in one or more of these areas: Climate Budget & Finance, Clean Transportation, Clean Electricity Affordability, and Insurance & Climate Resilience. The Senior Fellow works mainly with the Governor’s office and state agencies, in coordination with Climate Cabinet’s policy leadership, Policy Leads, the Texas team, and national team.

Deliverables - (to be prioritized with the Senior Fellow based on agreed hours)

• Strategy & workplan. Deliver a year-long workplan with goals, milestones, and decision points. Lead the research behind it, flag emerging opportunities and risks to Climate Cabinet’s policy team, and share progress updates every two weeks.

• Executive-branch engagement. Build relationships with the Governor’s office, state agencies, and local leaders, and work with them directly on policy development and issue education. Facilitate meetings and provide recommendations and technical support that lead to executive action.

• Policy analysis & materials. Produce expert memos, budget and finance analyses, briefings, and other materials for policymakers, coalition partners, and media.

• Representation & public narrative. Represent Climate Cabinet with officials, coalition partners, funders, and other audiences, and serve as a public voice on this work in coordination with Climate Cabinet’s communications team. Work with our policy, data, and communications teams on research and storytelling that put Texas on the map.

• Fundraising support. Support fundraising for this work in partnership with Climate Cabinet’s Development team, such as joining funder meetings and contributing to proposals and reports.

• Impact tracking & reporting. Keep a weekly impact tracker, and deliver an interim and a final impact report for national and state audiences.

• Executive-branch playbook. Document the approaches, tools, and lessons from this work in a playbook Climate Cabinet can use to expand executive-branch work to other states.

• Coordination. Join weekly and as-needed check-ins with Climate Cabinet’s policy and Texas teams to align on strategy and share what you’re learning.

Applicant Requirements

We’re looking for a senior policy strategist who can work with high autonomy, drive strategy in a complex political environment, and communicate clearly across audiences.

• Deep policy expertise. A Master’s degree or equivalent experience in climate-relevant financial, economic, regulatory, or public policy, including a strong understanding of state budgets and executive authority in Texas. Specific expertise in at least one of the four priority areas. You connect technical policy design to real-world climate and political goals, and help others understand the stakes and tradeoffs.

• Texas government and political experience. Experience in Texas government, executive-branch policy, lobbying, coalition work, and/or Texas politics. You understand how change happens through the Governor’s office and state agencies, and where state and city efforts can advance together in today’s political landscape.

• Track record of turning strategy into outcomes. You don’t just analyze policy; you define a path forward and move it into action. You build trust, guide others through complexity, and move relationship-driven work forward with urgency and care.

• Strong research and writing. You produce memos, briefings, and analyses that influence decision-makers and coalition strategy.

• Strong communicator and connector. You translate complex policy into clear, compelling language for officials, local leaders, coalition partners, press, funders, and Climate Cabinet’s team, and you align people around shared goals.

• Mission-driven with a growth mindset. You’re motivated by the urgency of climate action and by equitable solutions that lower costs for Texans. You seek feedback, keep learning, and see iteration as part of the work, which matters in an engagement that is testing a new approach for Climate Cabinet.

• Independent leadership within an agreed scope. You work independently within the agreed scope of the contract while coordinating closely with Climate Cabinet leadership on strategy and priorities.

Application Process
We are accepting applications via Greenhouse on a rolling basis with a priority deadline of December 4, 2026. Include a resume, writing sample, and a proposal (no more than 2-3 pages) that includes the following:

• Introduction and relevant experience What about Climate Cabinet and this engagement is appealing to you? A description of your experience and skills that satisfy the requirements of this role. An example of how you’ve advanced a policy change through a state executive branch, such as a governor’s office, state agency, or budget process, or through a similar venue. What was the opportunity, who did you engage, what strategy did you use, and what happened? Where you are located now, and your ability to be based in Texas and spend at least 40% of the time in Austin (including relocation if needed).

• Recommended approach for this scope of work: Your proposed design for this year-long effort. Include the policy area(s) you’d focus on, the key actions you’d pursue, and the stakeholders and decision-makers you’d engage.

• Estimated timeline of milestones for the year

• Availability: earliest start date and estimated hours per week

• Proposed rate and fee structure

• 2–3 References

• AI use: A brief note on whether and how you used AI in your proposal and/or writing sample. Using AI won’t disqualify you.

Writing sample: Please upload a writing sample that you are proud of and is reflective of the skills and experience required of this role. This is NOT a cover letter.

All applications submitted through December 4 will be reviewed and candidates will receive updates on their candidacy no later than December 18. The interview process will include approximately 2 Zoom interviews with the hiring manager and members of our team, and reference checks. Target contract start date is early January, 2027.

No obligation to contract:This request for proposal does not obligate Climate Cabinet to contract for services specified herein.
Rejection of proposals: Climate Cabinet reserves the right at its sole discretion to reject any and all proposals received without penalty and not to issue a contract as a result of this request for proposal.

You should apply! We encourage applications from people of color, members of the LGBTQ community, women, first-gen and low-income people, and members of marginalized communities.

Climate Cabinet is an equal opportunity employer. Climate Cabinet believes every employee has the right to work in an environment free from unlawful discrimination. Consistent with applicable federal, state and local laws, Climate Cabinet provides all employees and applicants with equal opportunity in all aspects of the employment relationship. This includes employment decisions related to hiring, promotions, transfers, disciplinary action, termination, and training. Climate Cabinet will comply with all applicable laws prohibiting discrimination in employment.

Want to learn more about Climate Cabinet? Check out our recent interview on Volts and climatecabinet.org

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. jobs.title: Senior Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Invisible

Invisible is an Applied AI research company closing the gap between frontier models and the enterprise. We provide the platform infrastructure that makes AI work in production at scale: unify fragmented data, map complex processes, orchestrate and evaluate agents, and stand up hyper-personalized workflow applications fast for companies like Grubhub, Alliance Global, and Thomson Reuters. Where models fall short, we build RL environments and data to fix them. The result: a virtuous cycle between enterprise deployment and model training.

Recognized as Best Predictive Analytics Platform of the Year at the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards, Invisible makes AI work.

About The Role

We’re seeking top product talent to embed with strategic enterprise clients in financial services, where modern technology like AI is changing how capital markets work. You will sit shoulder-to-shoulder with business stakeholders, translate ambiguous ideas into AI-powered solutions, and shepherd projects from discovery through delivery. A core focus of this role is the developer platforms and tools the client’s engineers rely on every day: you’ll help shape those tools from the ground up and see their impact across the whole organization. Over the next six months, your work will double discovery capacity, develop custom products leveraging AI, unlock new revenue streams for our clients and Invisible, and lay the groundwork for deeper, long-term partnerships.

This is a rare chance to bring a product mindset to developer experience at one of the most influential firms in finance, working on high-visibility projects with a team that wants to move fast.

What You’ll Do

• Discovery & Scoping: Lead concise, high-impact workshops that surface true business needs, define success metrics, and craft phased, right-sized scopes.

• Developer Experience: Own the roadmap for internal developer platforms and tooling — understand what slows engineers down, and build products they actually want to adopt.

• Project Stewardship: Build and own delivery timelines and OKRs, run stand-ups, clear blockers, coordinate directly with engineering teams to advance outcomes, and escalate early to keep work on track.

• Stakeholder Management: Act as the primary product point of contact for strategic enterprise clients, nurturing executive relationships and ensuring alignment.

• AI-Enabled Solution Design: Combine client context with Invisible’s AI toolkit to architect solutions using classical automation, GenAI, and human-in-the-loop approaches.

• Continuous Improvement: Document playbooks, mentor new analysts/PMs, and feed insights back into Invisible’s product and sales teams.

What We Need

Required:

• 5+ years in product management, solution consulting, or comparable delivery roles.

• Experience building products for developers — APIs, SDKs, developer platforms, or internal tooling — or a PM background that grew out of developer relations, developer advocacy, or solutions engineering.

• Demonstrated ability to turn ambiguous problems into shipped products or pilots.

• Proven success managing enterprise client relationships.

• High emotional intelligence and excellent communication skills.

• Extremely high level of personal ownership, entrepreneurial drive, and independence.

• Adaptable, resilient, curious, ambitious, coachable, low ego critical thinker.

• Comfortable in a high rate-of-change, evolving, ambiguous environment.

• Working knowledge of software architecture, APIs, and data flows; curiosity about GenAI.

• Familiarity with Agile methodologies and tools (Jira, Notion, Asana).

• Experience working in highly matrixed, enterprise organizations across multiple stakeholders.

• Authorization to work in the US and willingness to travel.

• Ability to work in-person, in-office in NYC 2-3 days per week.

Nice-to-have:

• Financial services or capital markets experience, especially building developer-facing products in that environment.

• Deep experience deploying AI/ML solutions in enterprise or regulated environments (e.g., financial services).

• Experience advising and partnering with senior stakeholders.

• Prior success scaling hybrid vendor-client teams or launching joint-venture initiatives.

What’s In It For You

Invisible is committed to fair and competitive pay, ensuring that compensation reflects both market conditions and the value each team member brings. Our salary structure accounts for regional differences in cost of living while maintaining internal equity.

The annual salary range for this position is: $164,000 - $212,000

Bonus and equity is included in all full-time, non commission offers. Final compensation is determined by a combination of factors, including location, job-related experience, skills, knowledge, internal pay equity, and overall market conditions. Because of this, every offer is unique. Additional details on total compensation and benefits will be discussed during the hiring process.

You can find more information about our geographic pay tiers here. During the interview process, your Invisible Talent Acquisition Partner will confirm which tier applies to your location. For candidates outside the U.S., compensation is adjusted to reflect local market conditions and cost of living.

What It's Like to Work at Invisible:

At Invisible, we’re not just redefining work—we’re reinventing it. We operate at the intersection of advanced AI and human ingenuity, pushing the boundaries of what’s possible to unlock productivity and scale. Ownership is at the core of everything we do. Here, you won’t just execute tasks—you’ll build, innovate, and shape the future alongside world-class clients pushing the boundaries of AI.

We expect bold ideas, relentless drive, and the ability to turn ambiguity into opportunity. The pace is fast, the challenges are big, and the growth is unmatched. We’re not for everyone, and we’re okay with that. If you’re looking for predictable routines, this isn’t the place for you. But if you’re driven to create, thrive in dynamic environments, and want a front-row seat to the AI revolution, you’ll fit right in.

Invisible is a hybrid organization with offices and team members located around the world. While some roles may offer remote flexibility, most positions involve in-office collaboration and are tied to specific locations. Any location-based requirements or hybrid expectations will be communicated by our Talent Acquisition team during the recruiting process.

Our hiring team thoughtfully uses AI to support an efficient, engaging, and inclusive interview process. Since AI can also be a helpful tool for candidates, we've outlined expectations for using it ethically throughout your interview journey. Click here to learn more about how we use AI and our guidelines for candidates.

If you require an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please submit your request using our accommodation request form. A member of our team will follow up to support your request.

Equal Opportunity Statement:
We’re an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law.

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer - Fraud
jobs.description:
We believe that the way people interact with their finances will drastically improve in the next few years. We’re dedicated to empowering this transformation by building the tools and experiences that thousands of developers use to create their own products. Plaid powers the tools millions of people rely on to live a healthier financial life. We work with thousands of companies like Venmo, SoFi, several of the Fortune 500, and many of the largest banks to make it easy for people to connect their financial accounts to the apps and services they want to use. Plaid’s network covers 12,000 financial institutions across the US, Canada, UK and Europe. Founded in 2013, the company is headquartered in San Francisco with offices in New York, Seattle, Washington D.C., Raleigh, London, and Amsterdam.

The Fraud Data team at Plaid builds the machine learning systems that power Plaid’s fraud detection products, leveraging insights from across Plaid’s network to help identify and stop fraud before it happens. Our team works across the full data science and machine learning lifecycle—from discovering new signals and experimenting with models to deploying and optimizing them in production. We continuously learn from real-world model performance and customer feedback to improve our systems and develop new ways to protect customers and consumers from evolving fraud threats.

As a Senior Machine Learning Engineer on Plaid's Fraud Data team, you will develop models that improve fraud detection for our customers. You will identify predictive patterns in Plaid's network data and lead projects from initial experiments through model deployment and ongoing improvement.

 - Investigate fraud patterns and model errors to identify new signals, improve detection, and expand coverage across customers and use cases.

 - Develop training datasets and predictive features, addressing challenges such as incomplete labels, class imbalance, data leakage, and changing fraud behavior.

 - Design, train, and tune models using traditional and modern ML methods, including gradient-boosted trees and neural networks, and evaluate newer architectures against existing approaches.

 - Design experiments to test features and models, comparing performance across time periods and customer segments using agreed detection and false-positive metrics.

 -  Build data and training pipelines that support reproducible experiments and efficient iteration on features and models.

 - Deploy models with Engineering and ML Infrastructure partners, balancing detection quality, latency, cost, and reliability.

 - Independently lead ML projects, agreeing on priorities and evaluation metrics with Data Science and Product and coordinating work through model release.

Responsibilities:

 - Take models from initial experimentation through production and evaluate their impact using real-world customer outcomes.

 - Strong ML and statistical fundamentals, including feature engineering, experiment design, model evaluation, and diagnosing why a model underperforms.

 - Strong understanding of the strengths, limitations, and applications for both traditional and modern ML methods, including gradient-boosted trees and neural networks.

 - Experience constructing training datasets and addressing label quality, data leakage, class imbalance, and generalization across time periods or populations.

 - Strong Python skills, SQL proficiency for working with training and evaluation data, and hands-on experience with ML frameworks such as PyTorch, scikit-learn, XGBoost, or equivalents.

 - Experience developing models that generalize across customers with different data and behavior patterns.

 - Experience using graph-based systems to extract predictive signals, uncover fraud patterns, and improve fraud model performance.

jobs.title: Head of Treasury
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As the Head of Treasury at Varda, you will own the company's cash, investments, banking, working capital, and insurance, and build the function that runs them. Varda builds a highly-engineered physical product: a bus, a capsule, and a payload that fly to orbit, manufacture, and come home. Behind that work sits more than $500 million of cash and investments, and this seat is where it is positioned, invested, forecast, banked, and insured.

Here's the scope. A board-approved investment policy, run in the order counterparty limits, then duration and liquidity tiers, then yield, with outside managers selected and operated under it. A cash forecast the executive team plans against. The bank structure: a market check you run, a recommendation you make, and the accounts, signatories, and entitlements you then administer. Working capital, coordinated end to end. The corporate insurance program: launch, reentry, and third-party liability, property and equipment, directors and officers, and the broader casualty program, with the broker, the placements, the renewals, the certificates, and the claims. The policies and controls that hold all of it together.

You own the framing. For every structural decision in treasury you do the analysis, bring three options and a recommendation, and take it for approval as the policy requires. Approved, or sent back with reasons; nobody rewrites your work. You carry the risk picture, counterparty, liquidity, operational, and insured, and you raise what matters before anyone asks.

The executive team plans against your forecast every month, mission and facility owners fly and build under coverage you placed, the money that funds every vehicle sits where you put it, and the auditors rely on controls you documented. That is the job.

This seat is for someone who has built a treasury function at a venture-backed or growth-stage company and wants to do it again at larger scale: the operator who builds the forecast, reads the bank agreements, and designs the renewal personally, and then brings the decision rather than the question.

Responsibilities

Invest the cash under policy

• Run the board-approved investment policy day to day in its order of priority, counterparty limits, then duration and liquidity tiers, then yield, and frame every revision as options and a recommendation.

• Select, onboard, and operate outside investment managers and custodians, set the mandates, move cash by liquidity tier, and report compliance monthly.

Know where the cash is and where it is going

• Build and run the 13-week cash forecast and the daily cash position, and keep the longer liquidity view current against the company's next milestones.

• Coordinate working capital end to end: targets, terms, and the monthly review, with DSO, DPO, and DIO reported on your cadence.

Build the bank platform

• Define the bank structure, including concentration, run the market check, and recommend; then administer the accounts, signatories, entitlements, connectivity, and documentation.

• Design the separation of duties for payments and transfers, so that administering an account, releasing a payment, and reconciling it are never in the same hands.

• Administer any credit facility, equipment financing, letter of credit, or guarantee the company puts in place: drawdowns, repayments, availability, issuance and renewals, and the reporting the agreements require.

Insure what we fly and what we build

• Own the corporate insurance program: launch, reentry, and third-party liability, property and equipment, directors and officers, and the broader casualty program.

• Design the program structure and the renewal strategy, run the broker relationship, placements, certificates, and claims, and set coverage requirements for every mission and facility with the people accountable for them.

• Keep the renewal calendar and the premium budget, and report the program's cost and structure into the company's capital planning.

Build controls that hold up

• Write the treasury policies and procedures and document the controls to a standard an auditor relies on.

• Choose the treasury technology and bank connectivity the function needs as it scales, and build it so it runs without you in the room.

What You Will Deliver

At the end of year one, Varda's cash is invested under a policy you run, forecast to a published accuracy, banked in a structure you recommended, and insured under a program you designed.

• In your first 60 days: the cash position and forecast running; investment managers selected on your recommendation and onboarding under way; the bank accounts, signatories, and entitlements inventoried; and the insurance program and its renewal in your hands.

• By the end of your first quarter: cash deployed under the policy with the first monthly compliance report delivered; the renewal placed under a structure you recommended; and the bank structure recommended and approved.

• By June 2027: the backup bank open and the accounts rationalized; working capital targets and terms approved and reviewed monthly; and the treasury policy set approved.

• By the end of 2027: controls documented and walked through with the auditors; forecast accuracy within an agreed tolerance; and the first revision of the investment policy framed and approved.

Basic Qualifications

• Built a treasury function from the ground up, or rebuilt one, at a venture-backed or growth-stage company, and ran it afterwards.

• Ran a cash and investment portfolio of $500 million or more under a board-approved investment policy, including the selection and day-to-day operation of outside investment managers.

• Ran a corporate insurance program end to end: renewals, broker management, placements, and claims.

• Ran bank operations and at least one bank selection, from structure to transition.

• Framed structural decisions for a CFO as options and a recommendation, and carried them through approval.

• Ten or more years in treasury or closely related corporate finance roles, the most recent running the function.

• Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, or another quantitative field.

• This full-time position requires 100% onsite work in El Segundo CA.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Launch or satellite insurance placed, or a specialist broker run in a market that was new to you.

• Treasury in hardware, aerospace, or defense, including letters of credit, surety, or performance bonds for government contracts.

• Treasury through an IPO or at a public company.

• Lender reporting and covenant compliance on a live credit facility.

• Designed cash concentration and pooling structures, including intercompany funding across entities.

• CTP or CFA.

Pay Range

• Salary Range: $200,000 - $240,000/per year

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

E-Verify Statement

Varda Space Industries, Inc. participates in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security E-Verify program. The E-Verify program is an Internet-based employment eligibility verification system operated by the U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. Learn more about the E-Verify program.

Candidates and employees are always evaluated based on merit, qualifications, and performance. We will never discriminate on the basis of race, color, gender, national origin, ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, martial status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status.

About This Role

As the Head of Cost Accounting at Varda, you will build the cost accounting function for a company that manufactures in orbit and lands its products back on Earth, and you will build it from the ground up.

Varda designs, builds and flies its W-Series vehicles in-house: the satellite bus, the reentry capsule, the heat shield and the pharmaceutical payload. We are moving from a few missions a year to a steady flight cadence, serving pharmaceutical, defense and research customers under commercial and government contracts, and standing up new production and laboratory space to do it. No one has run a factory whose output flies to orbit, processes a drug in microgravity and comes home through the atmosphere at hypersonic speed. So no one has built the cost accounting for one either. That is the job.

Here’s the scope. What a bus, a capsule, and a payload cost to build. What each mission costs to fly, by customer and by business line. How labor, material and overhead move from the production floor, the lab and the engineering teams onto missions and contracts. The indirect rate structure and timekeeping that qualify Varda for cost-type government contracts. The data pipelines that replace manual effort. And the roadmap, selection and implementation of the cost system Varda will run on for the next decade. You decide how it is done, and then you do it.

The impact lands everywhere. Your numbers inform which capsule configuration we build next, tell Manufacturing and Supply Chain where cost is moving and why, qualify Varda for a class of government contracts, and hold up under an external audit. The CFO, the Controller, the Production and Supply Chain leaders, Programs and the executive team will use what you build every month.

This is a seat for someone who has built cost accounting at a company that makes physical product and wants to do it again with far more scale, higher stakes and the freedom to do it right. If you have been running cost accounting inside someone else’s design and keeping a list of what you would do differently, this is where you get to find out.

Responsibilities

Establish the baseline

• Assess the cost baseline: cost of revenue, inventory and deferred launch cost balances by mission, reconciled to the general ledger, documented, and supported through the year-end audit, working with our finance partners and our government cost accounting specialists.

• Establish inception-to-date cost by vehicle and by mission.

Know what every vehicle and every mission costs

• Build and maintain the cost of a bus, a capsule, a heat shield and a payload: bills of material, labor, overhead, and the variance analysis that tells Production, Supply Chain and Engineering where cost is moving and why.

• Set cost targets and report actuals against them every month.

Design and run the allocation engine

• Design the cost pools, allocation bases and overhead absorption methodology, and run the monthly allocation cycle in a controlled model: locked templates, reconciliation to the ledger, results reflected in Business Central, and an audit trail for material moved between projects.

• Move each piece of the model into Business Central, Power BI or the long-term system as the data foundation matures.

Own inventory, work in process and deferred launch costs

• Own inventory valuation, work in process, cycle count and physical inventory results with Supply Chain, the capitalization and release of mission costs under our accounting policies, and the recoverability assessment of deferred costs by mission.

• Write the cost accounting policies: inventory, overhead absorption at normal capacity, classification of cost between cost of revenue, R&D and SG&A, deferred launch costs, and the right application of standard costing for our vehicles.

Qualify Varda for cost-type government contracts

• With our government cost accounting specialists, design the indirect rate structure, the allowability screening and the written cost accounting practices required for cost-type government contracts, and bring the accounting system through an SF 1408 review.

• Own provisional billing rates, the incurred cost submission, and the working relationship with DCAA and DCMA auditors.

Put labor where it belongs

• Define the timekeeping policy (daily entry, employee certification, supervisor approval, audit trail) and implement the timekeeping system and labor distribution in partnership with Enterprise Applications, Engineering, Production and the People team, so labor lands on missions and contracts from the source.

Automate, and own the roadmap

• Design, with Enterprise Applications, the project, mission and contract dimensions in Business Central, our MRP, our procurement tool and our spend platform so every dollar carries a charge number from the day it is incurred.

• Build the pipelines that bring ledger, MRP and timekeeping data into the cost model, and replace manual steps as fast as the data allows.

• Write the long-term cost accounting system and process roadmap, lead the requirements and selection of the long-term project costing solution, and act as the business owner of the implementation.

Build controls that hold up

• Own the control design and evidence for everything above: reconciliations, review sign-offs, methodology documentation, and the workpapers our external auditors and government auditors will test, built to the standard of a public company.

What You Will Deliver

By the end of your first year, cost accounting at Varda is a system: a documented methodology, a controlled monthly cycle, an auditable record for every mission, and the rate structure that qualifies Varda for cost-type government contracts. The milestones on the way:

• In your first 60 days: a complete baseline of cost of revenue, inventory and deferred launch costs by mission, a prioritized plan, and ownership of the monthly allocation cycle alongside our specialists and finance partners.

• By the end of your first quarter: cost balances reconciled, documented and supported for the year-end audit, with cost by mission for every flight.

• By June 2027: the allocation methodology documented and the monthly cycle under control; timekeeping and labor distribution live; the accounting system ready for an SF 1408 review; and a written recommendation on the long-term system, with requirements.

• By the end of 2027: provisional billing rates and incurred cost readiness, cost accounting policies approved, the right application of standard costing determined and in use, and the long-term system selected and in implementation.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance or a related field.

• 8+ years of progressive accounting experience, with at least 4 years owning cost accounting or manufacturing accounting (inventory, work in process, standard costs, overhead absorption, variances) at a company that builds a highly-engineered physical product.

• You have built or rebuilt a cost accounting function at a fast-growing hardware company, not only operated one: you designed the cost structure, the allocation methodology and the close process yourself.

• You have built overhead absorption and cost allocation models from a trial balance and run them month after month with reconciliations and review evidence.

• Hands-on experience in a mid-market or project costing ERP and a working understanding of how inventory, MRP, timekeeping, payroll and the general ledger fit together.

• Direct experience supporting an external audit of inventory, cost of revenue and capitalized costs, including producing the workpapers.

• Advanced Excel and at least one of Power Query, SQL or Power BI; comfortable building the data pipeline rather than waiting for one.

• This full-time position requires 100% onsite work in El Segundo CA.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Government contract cost accounting: FAR Part 31, indirect rate structures, DCAA audits, SF 1408 reviews, incurred cost submissions and DFARS timekeeping requirements. You will build this with specialist support, so exposure matters more than depth; having been through a DCAA audit or an SF 1408 review is a strong plus.

• Cost accounting for long-cycle, project-based or mission-based builds (spacecraft, launch vehicles, aircraft, defense systems, shipbuilding), including deferred and contract fulfillment costs.

• Experience at a venture-backed hard-tech company moving from prototype to production.

jobs.title: Director, Accounting
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As the Director, Accounting at Varda, you will own the general ledger and the monthly close for a company that designs, builds, flies, and recovers a highly-engineered physical product. Because Varda makes its vehicles in-house, the ledger carries inventory, fixed assets and construction in progress, deferred launch costs, government contracts, and commercial pharmaceutical programs at the same time, and every one of them has to be right every month. You will sit at the center of a finance organization built around the close: a controllership, financial planning, and specialist seats in cost, treasury, and government accounting, all of which run on your ledger.

Here's the scope. The monthly close in Business Central, from the calendar to the lock. Balance sheet reconciliations, every account, every month. The close calendar and the standards every sub-ledger closes to: payables, payroll, fixed assets, and inventory. The fixed asset and inventory records for a production facility and a growing capital program. Customer billing and collections. The accounting requirements for every system that feeds the ledger. Audit readiness: the reconciliations and support behind every balance, the request list, the room. Controls that hold up under an outside tester. A team of accountants to lead and develop.

Every budget owner at Varda will plan and manage on the actuals you lock. Executives review their numbers against plan by day ten of each month and the CEO sees the company by day twelve, and that cadence runs on a close that is done on day five. The auditors work from your reconciliations.

This seat is for a CPA who has run the close at a company that makes physical product, has taken a close from loose to locked and kept it there, has sat across the table from a Big Four auditor as the company's owner of the audit, and wants to build the next one from the ground up with a team of their own. You get what finance needs from scientists and engineers whose first priority is the mission, and you can explain a number to a department head without jargon.

Responsibilities

Close the books in five days

• Run the monthly close in Business Central: the calendar, the checklist, the cutoff, the reconciliations, the preparer and reviewer control, and the lock.

• Set the close calendar and the standards every sub-ledger closes to, and hold them: cutoff, accrual methodology, sub-ledger to ledger reconciliation, and support.

• Deliver a trial balance that is final on day five, with department actuals by account and by vendor, the functional split applied by a written method, and flux commentary that starts from the entry log.

Keep a ledger that is final when the month is

• Reconcile every balance sheet account every month, complete and reviewed: cash, accrued liabilities, prepaids, fixed assets and construction in progress, inventory, deferred revenue, deferred launch costs, and payroll liabilities.

• Maintain one journal source and one entry log, with a preparer, a reviewer, support, and a reason on every entry.

• Book the entries the accounting policies call for in the periods they belong to, with workpapers that stand on their own.

Keep the sub-ledgers right

• Keep the fixed asset and construction in progress records: capitalization applied by policy, in-service dates, depreciation, and the roll forward, tied to the capital register.

• Keep the inventory records: the sub-ledger, counts, the tie from the manufacturing system to the ledger, and reserves.

• Book and reconcile payroll by department each cycle, record stock-based compensation each quarter under the written policy, and run customer billing and collections.

Make the seam with payables hold

• Determine the accrual methodology and the unrecorded liabilities search with the payables leader, and reconcile the payables sub-ledger and the card platform to the ledger every cycle.

• Decide how coding is reviewed before the trial balance is struck, so the close does not end in post-close entries.

Build controls that hold up

• Own audit readiness in the ledger: the request list, the reconciliations and support behind every balance, the schedule, and the room.

• Document the approval matrices, segregation of duties in the ERP, the reconciliation standard, and a close checklist an outside tester could follow.

• Write the procedures for every account the seat touches, so the close runs the same way whoever runs it.

Own the accounting requirements for the systems that feed the ledger

• Define the account and department dictionary, the dimension master, posting-date controls, and user roles, and test what the systems teams build.

• Own the accounting side of every interface into the ledger: payroll, the card platform, invoice automation, and the manufacturing system.

Lead the team

• Hire, develop, and review the accountants on the team, and set the standard for workpapers, reconciliations, and documentation.

• Bring in outside support for volume when it is needed, and bring the work back in-house with documentation when it is done.

What You Will Deliver

By the end of your first year, the books close hard in five business days every month, every balance sheet account is reconciled and reviewed monthly, the annual audit is supported on the auditor's schedule, and the controls are documented well enough that an outside tester could follow them.

• In your first 60 days: you have run one close end to end, you know every balance sheet account's owner and reconciliation status, you have met the auditor and the teams that administer the systems, and the close calendar and the sub-ledger standards are written and agreed.

• By the end of your first quarter: the close runs in five business days and locks, with a documented reason for anything that moves after; balance sheet reconciliations are complete and reviewed monthly; the audit request list is issued and tracked.

• By June 2027: the annual audit is supported through fieldwork, with the reconciliations and support behind every balance delivered on the auditor's schedule; payables, payroll, fixed assets, and inventory close by day three; the team runs the mechanics of the close.

• By the end of 2027: every month of the year closed hard in five days; department actuals by account and by vendor that budget owners trust; the approval matrices, segregation of duties, reconciliation standard, and close checklist documented; procedures written for every account; the payroll interface to the ledger in place.

Basic Qualifications

• An active CPA.

• Ten or more years in accounting, including at least three leading the monthly close at a company that makes a highly-engineered physical product, with inventory, fixed assets, and construction in progress on the balance sheet.

• Has taken a close to a week or less and kept it there, with the calendar, the checklist, the reconciliation standard, and the preparer and reviewer control to show for it.

• Company-side owner of an annual audit with a Big Four or national firm, including the remediation of a control finding through to a clean opinion.

• Working knowledge of the standards this ledger applies every month: revenue recognition (ASC 606), leases (ASC 842), stock-based compensation (ASC 718), inventory and contract costs (ASC 330 and ASC 340-40), and fixed assets and capitalization (ASC 360), with the judgment to know when a transaction needs a position paper rather than an entry.

• Has rebuilt a chart of accounts, converted an ERP, or carried a ledger through a restatement, with workpapers an auditor accepted.

• Has run payables or worked daily with a payables leader where most spend runs on cards and on purchase orders with three-way match.

• Has hired and developed accountants, and has written procedures that outlived them.

• Hands-on in a mid-market ERP, and comfortable working through large datasets with queries, scripts, or AI tools.

• This full-time position requires 100% onsite work in El Segundo CA.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• A public accounting foundation in audit at a Big Four or national firm.

• Experience closing the books in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.

• Has seen SOX readiness or a controls build from the company side.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
ABOUT CLARION

Clarion is the first system built to run the whole medical practice. Revenue is up 10x in a year, we have eight-figure contracted revenue, and this fall we signed the two largest contracts in our history. We're a team of 20, and the people who join now will define what Clarion becomes.



Medical practices are at a breaking point

Reimbursement is falling, costs are rising, and patients are falling through the cracks.

 - Medicare pays practices 33% less than it did in 2001, after adjusting for practice costs (AMA).

 - 84% of practices say operating costs are up again this year. Fewer than half say revenue is (MGMA).

 - In one large health system, only 35% of specialist referrals ended in a completed visit (Journal of General Internal Medicine).



What we do

Every practice runs on rules that live in schedulers' heads and on sticky notes behind the front desk. We take the time to learn those rules. Then our AI agents follow them to handle calls, referrals, and scheduling for specialty groups and value-based care organizations, and document the work in the EHR. Staff get their time back for the work that needs a person.



Where we're going

We're building a new category of software, the practice operations platform, or POP. It's the biggest shift in how practices run since the EHR.

Within a few years, we believe every practice will run on just two systems. One is the electronic health record. The other is a practice operations platform, where AI agents handle the tasks people do by hand in the clinic today, from the first phone call to the final payment. The EHR is the source of truth for patient care. Clarion will be the source of truth for running the practice.

We started with calls, referrals, and scheduling. Billing, prior auth, and collections come next. We want Clarion to be as essential to every practice as its EHR, and we're hiring the people who will build it.



Why join now

 - Early, but de-risked. Revenue is up 10x year over year and we have eight-figure contracted revenue. Most of our growth for the next two quarters is already signed.

 - We win the biggest deals. This fall we signed the two largest contracts in our history. One is a three-year enterprise agreement with one of the largest GI groups in the country, won after a 15-vendor RFP and a head-to-head pilot. We win 80% of competitive head-to-head deals. Our customers also include a Fortune 500 payor and two of the five largest ACOs in the country.

 - The product works. Our AI agents handle more than 10 million patient calls a year for our customers. They resolve 60% of in-scope calls end to end and convert 70% of the referrals they work into booked visits.

 - We move fast. We launched 345 providers in Q3, three times the quarter before, and our fastest kickoff to go-live is under five days. Our customers span nearly 1,500 locations and more than 3,700 providers across 18 specialties.

 - The team. Clarion was founded by Ryan Gallagher, a Stanford- and Harvard-trained doctor on the founding team of two successful virtual care companies, and Jeff Lamothe, an ex-Amazon Alexa engineer who led AI/ML teams at Salesforce. We've raised $10M from Accel and Y Combinator, and the 20 of us work in person in Flatiron.



Why this role

 - The closest thing to a founder's seat. You'll report to Ryan Gallagher, our CEO, and work on whatever matters most to the company that week. You'll see how every part of a fast-growing company gets built. If you want to start or run a company someday, this is the best training we know of.

 - You'll own real outcomes. You'll own projects that change the company, like how we price, how we get paid, and how we plan, and you'll take on the hardest problems that have no owner. At 10x growth, the work gets bigger every quarter.

 - The role grows as fast as you do. We expect the person in this seat to outgrow it. Great chiefs of staff go on to run a function or start a company of their own, and we want to hire someone with that ambition.



What you'll do

 - Operating rhythm. Keep the weekly leadership meeting, the Friday whole-team business review, quarterly planning, and company OKRs on track. Own the metrics, the pre-reads, and follow-through on every decision.

 - Finance and business operations. Own billing and collections, the monthly close with our accounting partner, the operating model and budget, banking, and the cap table.

 - Deal desk. Work with sales on pricing approvals, order forms, redlines, and renewals. Own vendor contracts and spend.

 - Board and investors. Prepare board materials and investor updates, keep the data room current, and support our next fundraise.

 - Special projects. Take problems with no clear owner, scope them, solve them, and hand them to a permanent owner. Pricing changes, a new office, and first-time company policies are the kind of work we mean.

 - CEO leverage. Manage Ryan's priorities and time, prep him for key customer and investor meetings, and close the loops he opens.



What we're looking for

 - A few years of experience running things. You've owned a project, a process, or a team from start to finish, whether at a startup, in consulting or banking, or in a company of your own. Healthcare experience is a plus, not a requirement.

 - Versatile. You can move between a pricing model, a board deck, and a vendor dispute in one afternoon, and no task is beneath you.

 - Fast and responsive. You answer quickly, close loops the same day, and nothing you own goes quiet.

 - You work like a founder. You care about the outcome as much as we do and put in what the work takes.

 - You write clearly and briefly. Your memos get read and acted on.

 - Direct. You'll tell Ryan when he's wrong and bring a better answer.

 - Discretion with sensitive information, including compensation, contracts, and board matters.

 - Excited to work from our NYC office five days a week.



What we offer

 - Ownership. We care that everyone who joins has a meaningful ownership stake in the business.

 - Room to grow. We promote from within. Our Head of Engineering joined as an engineer.

 - A seat next to the CEO. You'll be in the room for every important decision the company makes.

 - Work you can see. Every practice we launch reaches more patients and gives staff hours back.

 - In person. We've worked together in person since day one. It's why we move fast.

 - Benefits. 100% covered health insurance, 401(k), parental leave, flexible time off, commuter benefits, team lunches, quarterly offsites, and monthly team events.
   
   

Interview process

We decide within 24 hours of each stage and update you shortly after.

 - Intro call. 15 minutes, virtual. A conversation about the role and your background.

 - Working session. 45 minutes, virtual. You'll work through a real operating problem with Ryan.

 - Experience interview. 30 minutes, virtual. We'll go deep on what you've owned and how you work.

 - Half-day onsite. In person in New York. A written exercise, time with the leadership team, and a feel for how we work.

If this sounds like you, we'd love to hear from you.

jobs.title: Senior Applications Engineer - CNC - Northeast
jobs.description:
About MISUMI Americas

MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.

Impact In This Role

Misumi Americas is seeking a Senior Applications Engineer - CNC to join our solution engineering team focused on strategic, high-complexity, production-level customer programs. This role sits at the intersection of engineering, manufacturing, customer advisory, and commercial execution, supporting customers as they scale from prototype into production.

The ideal candidate brings deep experience in CNC machining, casting, CAD, (SolidWorks), GD&T, and DFM skills, strong technical communication skills, and the ability to guide customers through DFM/DFA, production readiness, operational/program support, cost optimization, and mechanical assembly considerations. This role is mainly customer-facing and requires comfort operating in ambiguous, high-stakes environments.

What You’ll Be Doing

Customer & Program/Production Support

• Serve as a trusted technical advisor/guide for strategic customers with complex CNC manufacturing needs.

• Lead technical scoping discussions, translating customer requirements into manufacturable, scalable solutions.

• Some level of support for customers through prototype → production transitions, anticipating manufacturing risks early.

Manufacturing & DFM Expertise

• Perform detailed DFM/DFA reviews for CNC-machined components.

• Evaluate part geometry, tolerances, GD&T, material selection, and finish requirements for manufacturability and cost.

• Provide cost optimization recommendations based on process selection, feature simplification, and volume scaling.

• Support efforts with manufacturing-informed input on feasibility, risk, and lead time.

Assembly & System-Level Understanding/Support

• Evaluate and guide on mechanical assemblies, including:

• Part-to-part fit, stack-ups, and tolerance interactions

• Fastener selection, joint design, and access for assembly

• Assembly sequencing and installation considerations

• Help customers identify risks related to assembly, serviceability, and field installation.

• Provide feedback that improves downstream assembly efficiency and reduces rework.

Technical Execution

• Review and interpret engineering drawings with strong command of GD&T.

• Perform CAD work, including:

• Design updates for manufacturability

• Parametric 3D Modeling & Visualization

• Detailed Documentation & Drafting with GD&T

• Optimizing CAD — CNC to Casting and 3DP to IM

• Reverse engineering

• Collaborate cross-functionally with Sales, Operations, Quality, and LoB teams.

Quality & Compliance Awareness

• Apply working knowledge of ISO 9001 and AS9100D requirements in customer discussions and internal workflows.

• Identify quality risks early and ensure proper requirements definition (“quality in, quality out”).

Desired Traits

• 6+ years of relevant experience in manufacturing roles such as CNC (candidates with deeper experience are strongly encouraged to apply).

• Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing Engineering or related field, or equivalent demonstrated hands-on experience.

• Strong expertise in CNC machining processes (milling, turning, multi-axis) and Casting, .

• Must have DFM, cost optimization, and manufacturing trade-off fluency.

• Hands-on experience in production-scale manufacturing programs.

• Proven ability to interpret and apply engineering drawings and GD&T.

• Solid understanding of mechanical assemblies and installation considerations.

• Experience supporting customer-facing technical discussions.

• Familiarity with ISO 9001 and AS9100D compliance environments.

• Willingness and ability to travel 30–40%.

• Proficiency with Google Workspace and/or Microsoft Office.

• Strong verbal, written, and digital communication skills.

• SolidWorks CAD proficiency.

• Willingness to perform hands-on CAD work and reverse engineering as needed.

• Willingness to support the Marketing team with technical publications, seminars, university lectures, and other related activities as needed.

Nice-to-Have Qualifications

• Experience with Casting, Molding (IM) and/or Additive Manufacturing (3DP).

• Prior experience working with external suppliers or contract manufacturers.

• Leverage AI tools (e.g., Claude and other AI assistants) to accelerate DFM analysis, documentation, customer-facing content creation, and day-to-day engineering workflows.

• Experience integrating AI/LLM tools into engineering or customer-facing workflows.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

• Standard Office & Remote Work: Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer for remote customer consultations.

• Onsite Environments: Must be able to walk and stand on manufacturing floors and trade show environments for extended periods. Must be able to safely navigate industrial areas around heavy machinery and wear required PPE (safety glasses, safety shoes, hearing protection).

• Lifting & Handling: Ability to occasionally lift, move, and position mechanical parts, prototypes, or trade show materials weighing up to 30 lbs.

Perks and Benefits

• Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance

• 401K plan

• Parental leave programs

• Paid volunteer days

• And much, much more!

Salary Range: $125,000 to $142,000 per year, based upon experience

Interested in learning more?  We look forward to hearing from you soon.

We’re actively seeking teammates who:

• Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.

• Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.

• Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.

• Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.

• Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates

We encourage applications from members of underrepresented groups, including but not limited to women, members of the LGBTQ community, people of color, people with disabilities, and veterans.

jobs.title: Associate Manufacturing Engineer
jobs.description:
AST SpaceMobile and our global partners are building the first and only space-based cellular broadband network to be accessible by standard smartphones. Called SpaceMobile, this ultra-powerful network is being designed to provide connectivity at 4G/5G speeds everywhere on the planet – on land, at sea and in flight.

Position Overview

The Associate Manufacturing Engineer will support the development, evaluation, and continuous improvement of manufacturing methods and processes to sustain current production and support the introduction of new products. This role contributes to manufacturing readiness, process optimization, product quality, and the successful transition of products from design to production. The position works closely with Product Engineering, Quality, Operations, and Supply Chain to ensure manufacturable designs and robust production processes.

Key Responsibilities

• Assess new product concepts and designs for manufacturability, providing recommendations to R&D/Product Engineering.

• Develop methods and processes for manufacturing new products in the safest, most cost-effective manner while meeting quality standards and production demand.

• Conduct proof-of-principle or proof-of-concept studies to validate manufacturing approaches.

• Design detailed manufacturing processes, including layouts, tooling, fixtures, CNC programming support, testing, and documentation.

• Interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and GD&T requirements to ensure manufacturability and compliance with design intent.

• Support development of tooling, fixtures, gauges, and inspection methods to achieve production and quality objectives.

• Continuously improve existing production methods using Six Sigma methodologies and knowledge of product design, materials, fabrication processes, tooling, equipment capabilities, assembly techniques, and quality standards.

• Troubleshoot technical issues in current production and provide engineering support to operations.

• Participate in or lead Safety, Kaizen, and other continuous improvement initiatives.

• Support the qualification of new or modified products through manufacturing processes to final completion.

• Develop and maintain manufacturing work instructions, process documentation, and standardized operating procedures.

Qualifications

Education

• Bachelor’s Degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or related discipline OR 8 years of equivalent experience.

Experience

• 0–3 years of experience in a manufacturing environment.

• Proficient with MS Office and CAD/CAM tools.

• Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and GD&T.

• Basic understanding of manufacturing processes, tooling, fixtures, and quality systems.

Preferred Qualifications

• Working knowledge of GD&T (ASME Y14.5), tolerance stack-up concepts, and engineering drawing interpretation.

• Understanding of tooling, gauging, Six Sigma principles, capability studies, and statistical process control.

• Experience in technical writing, including procedures, work instructions, and manufacturing documentation.

• Exposure to process development and manufacturing engineering in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability production environments.

• Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI) and manufacturing process validation activities.

Soft Skills

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare instructions, procedures, and documentation.

• Strong organizational and project management abilities.

• Proven problem-solving skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across teams.

• Detail-oriented, structured, and able to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment.

• Ability to analyze technical data and make sound engineering recommendations.

Technology Stack

• MS Office Suite

• CAD/CAM software

• Manufacturing process design tools

• Data analysis or statistical process control tools (e.g., Minitab)

• PLM, ERP, or manufacturing execution systems (MES) preferred

Physical Requirements

• Ability to work in a standard office environment.

• Ability to work on the production floor as needed, including standing, walking, and interacting with equipment.

• Ability to use a computer for extended periods.

Benefits & Perks

• Competitive compensation package.

• Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance.
