jobs.title: Senior Director, AI Platforms
jobs.description:
About Flagship Pioneering:

Flagship Pioneering invents and builds platform companies, each with the potential for multiple products that transform human health, sustainability and beyond. Since its launch in 2000, Flagship has originated more than 100 companies. Many of these companies have addressed humanity’s most urgent challenges: vaccinating billions of people against COVID-19, curing intractable diseases, improving human health, preempting illness, and feeding the world by improving the resiliency and sustainability of agriculture.

Flagship has been recognized twice on FORTUNE’s “Change the World” list, an annual ranking of companies that have made a positive social and environmental impact through activities that are part of their core business strategies and has been twice named to Fast Company’s annual list of the World’s Most Innovative Companies. Learn more about Flagship at www.flagshippioneering.com.

At Flagship, we accept impossible missions to enable bigger leaps. Our core values guide us through uncertainty and toward lasting impact.

Position Summary:

The Senior Director, AI Platforms is IT’s senior-most technical individual contributor who leads the technology foundations for Flagship’s enterprise AI agenda. This technical leader turns enterprise priorities into a platform strategy, target architecture, operating model, and investment roadmap for shared models, agent infrastructure, connectivity, context, and standards.

Serving as IT’s engineering counterpart to Pioneering Intelligence (PI), this leader partners with PI, Information Security, Digital Platforms, business functions, and portfolio companies on foundational initiatives, decision rights, and governance.

What You'll Do:

Strategy and architecture

• Develop the multi-year enterprise AI platform technical strategy, investment roadmap, and outcomes for shared models, agents, connectivity, context, and engineering standards.

• Partner with PI and IT executive leadership to establish shared architecture principles, governance, funding, decision rights, and the path from experimentation to supported services.

• Own the enterprise AI reference architecture, co-developed with PI, and lead build-versus-buy decisions for gateways, data access, identity, observability, and security; bring IT’s run, cost, and supportability view to model and agent-runtime decisions.

Models and agents

• Own the enterprise AI gateway and model-routing strategy, including approved models and providers, policy- and cost-aware routing, credentials, spend controls, and resilience, with the ability to serve in-house models alongside commercial providers.

• Partner with PI to establish open-weight, open-source, and local model capabilities for sensitive, regional, or cost-sensitive workloads, with IT owning the path to supported production service.

• Partner with PI and scientific, legal, privacy, and security leaders on a life-sciences model path for bio-content and zero-data-retention requirements, with IT delivering governed workspaces and production support.

• Provide governed enterprise infrastructure for building and running agents, including identity, audit, human approvals, retrieval, evaluation, emergency controls, and portability, interoperable with science-specific agents. Support enterprise adoption and change management of the agent infrastructure.

Connect and context

• Own the enterprise Model Context Protocol (MCP) control plane and roadmap, including priorities, a risk-tiered connection inventory, vendor integrations, and custom services where needed, partnering with system owners on scientific connections.

• Establish governed connections to critical business systems, with human approval and logging for higher-risk agent actions.

• Lead the architecture and build-versus-buy direction for enterprise search and context that gives authorized users and agents access to governed company knowledge.

• Partner with PI and Digital Platforms to define the shared interfaces, dependencies, and service expectations for connectivity, context, governance, and data foundations needed to make AI successful.

Delivery and quality

• Establish evaluation frameworks and guidelines for models, agents, retrieval, and workflows, including tracing, quality, version management, and benchmarks based on Flagship business tasks.

• Define production-readiness, support, service measures, and the usage, cost, risk, and outcome data needed to assess value.

• Govern platform-dependent AI use cases, ensuring shared services, accountable owners, production readiness, and post-launch value measurement.

Reuse and standards

• Drive reuse of AI assets through an inner-source model for governed agents, skills, applications, connectors, code, and patterns, with clear contribution, ownership, documentation, and support standards.

• Design a secure development path for AI-assisted and citizen-built applications, including approved platforms and templates, access controls, automated deployment, secrets, testing, security review, and intake for externally exposed applications.

• Work with PI under a build-to-run model with shared intake, early architecture review, reusable services, named operational owners, and agreed criteria for moving capabilities to supported enterprise services.

• Scale adoption through self-service standards, automated policy and license checks, reference implementations, reusable skills, technical communities, and builder enablement.

Governance and security

• Co-define the technology governance model with PI, Enterprise AI, and Information Security, including decision rights, risk tiers, architecture standards, exceptions, and pre-approved patterns.

• Own AI security architecture, including agent identities and credentials, data boundaries, isolated execution, least-privilege access, safeguards against malicious instructions and data disclosure, and evidence for security review.

• Deliver security controls and evidence, including gateway policies, approved connections, AI inventory, zero-data-retention checks, audit logs, and detection of unapproved AI use. Lead the technology response to AI incidents in partnership with Cyber Security.

Platform operations and partnerships

• Establish triage, service ownership, automation, and performance measures for enterprise AI support, using service patterns to guide roadmap and capacity.

• Oversee administration and maintenance for enterprise AI platforms, including access, releases, production support, backup administration, and tested emergency access.

• Support Flagship Labs and portfolio companies through shared foundations, common standards, local accountability, and clear decision rights. Advise strategic partners and represent the platform strategy in enterprise forums.

• Build strong cross-functional partnerships across the Flagship ecosystem (particularly with PI, Information Security, and other functions within IT) to align platform decisions, security architecture, risk management, standards, and services under shared ownership.

What We're Looking For:

• 10+ years in technology engineering, architecture, or platform delivery, including experience leading cross-organizational technical initiatives through influence

• Success setting platform strategy, architecture, investment roadmaps, operating models, and measurable outcomes at enterprise scale.

• Deep knowledge of production AI platforms, including model routing, large language model APIs, agents, retrieval, evaluations, observability, and machine-learning operations.

• Experience with cloud architecture, enterprise integrations, APIs, identity and access management, security controls, and production operations.

• Track record aligning senior leaders on architecture, governance, funding, decision rights, and build-versus-buy choices.

• Sound judgment balancing speed, security, reliability, cost, supportability, and responsible AI.

• Ability to lead through influence, communicate technical tradeoffs to executives, and drive accountability across organizational boundaries.

Nice to Have

• Experience in life sciences, biotechnology, research, or another environment with sensitive or regulated data.

• Experience with MCP, agent runtimes, enterprise search, retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases, or enterprise context layers.

• Experience with citizen-development standards, reusable AI assets, and build-to-run models.

• Experience operating shared platforms across federated business units, labs, or portfolio companies.

Why This Role

Shape the shared foundations that determine how quickly and responsibly Flagship, its Labs, and portfolio companies can scale enterprise AI.

Join us and help change mental health care for children for the better!

You’ll build meaningful relationships with patients and families, taking the time to understand their needs, support engagement in treatment, and educate them on therapeutic approaches that foster long-term progress.

Working alongside an interdisciplinary team, you’ll be empowered to make a meaningful impact in the lives of young patients and their families through compassionate, evidence-based care.

jobs.description:
Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads.

Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter!

If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders.

Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light!

About this job

We are seeking an intern with a background and interest in Photonics and Laser packaging, optical design and hands-on laboratory experience. This internship offers a unique opportunity to bridge the gap between design, simulation and physical prototyping of next-generation photonic interfaces. You will be responsible for developing high-efficiency optical coupling solutions and establishing a multi-physics analysis methodology.

Responsibilities

• Design and build next-generation optical coupling solutions, contributing to optical simulations and hands-on prototyping of low-loss PIC-to-Fiber Array Unit (FAU) and lens array assemblies in the lab.

• Support process development for detachable, high-volume manufacturing-ready FAU technology

Minimum Qualifications

• Currently enrolled in a PhD or MS program in Optical Engineering, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field.

• Solid foundational understanding of optical coupling mechanics, materials and mode-matching physics.

• Strong documentation practices and effective communication of complex technical trade-offs to cross-functional teams.

• Proficiency in mechanical design and tolerance analysis with Solidworks.

• Proficiency in optical and/or structural simulation tools such as ANSYS Mechanical or Zemax.

Preferred Qualifications

• Hands-on experience with mode field characterization, multi-axis fiber and lens alignment systems, laser sources, and optical power meters.

• Familiarity with silicon photonics packaging methodologies, optical epoxies, and thermal-mechanical stress analysis.

• Experience with automated test routines (Python, MATLAB, or LabVIEW) for lab instrumentation control.

Our internship hourly rates are a standard pay determined based on the position and your location, year in school, degree, and experience.

jobs.title: 2027 Deployment Operations Intern
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril is fielding the next generation of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) to tackle the extremely challenging industry demands of seabed exploration. Anduril has brought to the market a unique, ultra-long-range, full-ocean-depth platform, and a completely refreshed maritime vehicle and flexible manufacturing architecture that scales from “large” to “extra-large” vehicle sizes. Today, Anduril is executing on multi-million-dollar contracts while simultaneously performing Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) AUV operations.

As our Maritime team continues to quickly grow, we are looking for motivated students who are inspired to work within an extremely energetic, creative, and innovative team that is passionate about subsea robotics and exploring the open ocean. We work in a highly dynamic environment where collaboration and idea sharing are a way of life.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Deployment Operations Intern to join our rapidly growing team in Quincy, MA. As an intern, you will support the team that gets our hardware into our customers’ hands and deploys our people to support their missions. You’ll get hands-on experience in real logistics work from day one.

The Logistics team has built a white glove service that develops and carries out Anduril’s strategy for delivering hardware and software to customers, often where the work is mission critical and logistically challenging. Working alongside experienced logistics team members, you will learn how shipments are planned, tracked, and delivered, and how teams work together to unblock issues. This internship is a chance to build a foundation in logistics, see how a fast-growing defense technology company operates, and contribute to projects that improve how our team works.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• Help keep vehicle and equipment records accurate and up to date in our tracking systems

• Support the team in coordinating with supply chain, operations, and outside partners to keep shipments moving on schedule

• Assist with shipment preparation and tracking for demos, deployments, and maintenance activities

• Help with the delivery of vehicles and equipment for demos, deployments, and exercises

• Support reverse logistics for Maritime hardware, including physical inventory counts when items return

• Spot gaps or inefficiencies in current logistics processes and suggest improvements

• Help track and organize spare parts records for deployments

• Own a defined intern project (for example, a process improvement, tracking tool, or documentation effort) and present your results at the end of the internship

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Must be pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, Operations, Engineering, or a related field.

• Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester.

jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Connected Warfare is the division at Anduril dedicated to the modernization of the global command and control systems of U.S. and Allied forces.  New technologies and new adversaries demand a new approach to battlefield intelligence, and our hardware and software products are rapidly scaling in production to deliver the volumes and capabilities that our customers need.  Our ecosystem enables connected warfare with disproportional impact by connecting every robot, human, and sensor in every domain, bringing together hundreds of thousands of end points across the globe.

As a Mechanical Engineer in Connected Warfare, you will be the driving force behind designing, building, and sustaining the physical systems that give soldiers on the front lines the computing, communications, and command and control capabilities they need to succeed and survive in any environment. If this sounds exciting to work towards, please learn more on our website here.

After reviewing our website above, please note that within Connected Warfare, our Menace-I and Menace-X teams are actively hiring Mechanical Engineers to work in our Costa Mesa, CA headquarters.  If these products look interesting and you're either already living in Orange County, CA, or are open to a paid relocation there, we invite you to read further to learn about the open roles on these teams!

WHAT YOU'LL DO

As a hands-on owner of hardware across its lifecycle, you'll take real technical ownership from concept through fielded, in-production systems. Your responsibilities will include:

* Own Hardware End-to-End: Take designs from concept generation through prototyping, qualification, production ramp, and sustained use in the hands of warfighters.
* Design From the Ground Up: Engineer novel hardware for demanding mission sets, sometimes starting from a blank sheet, and sometimes revising and improving existing designs as products evolve.
* Understand the Mission: Work directly with customers and internal stakeholders to understand real battlefield challenges and translate them into hardware that solves them.
* Engineer for Survival: Apply engineering first principles, analysis, and rigorous testing to ensure designs survive the harshest battlefield conditions and pass qualification campaigns.
* Get Hands-On: Build and iterate on prototypes and first articles yourself, moving quickly from idea to physical hardware.
* Resolve Production Issues: Investigate quality issues, drawing errors, and manufacturing challenges using root cause analysis (RCA) and permanent corrective action (PCA), and partner with manufacturing to feed design-for-manufacture-and-assembly (DFMA) improvements back into the design.
* Deliver at Scale: Partner with manufacturing and production teams to build and ship hardware at volume.
* Collaborative Innovation: Work day to day as part of a tight-knit product team alongside designers, manufacturing engineers, and production partners, moving fast in an environment of rapid iteration and technical excellence.

* 2-6 years of professional, post-graduate mechanical engineering experience.

* Strong CAD skills and the ability to produce high-quality engineering drawings and documentation.
* Demonstrated hands-on fabrication skills.

* Excitement to work onsite at our headquarters in Costa Mesa, CA the majority of the time!

* Experience with Siemens NX and Teamcenter PLM.
* Ability to integrate electronic components into mechanical designs (motors, controllers, sensors, etc.).
* Hands-on experience with machining, sheet metal, composites, and 3D printing.
* Knowledge of static, dynamic, or thermal analysis methods and their application in ANSYS.
* Experience managing products in medium- to high-volume production, including BOM ownership and formal change management across multiple configurations.
* Experience with root cause analysis (RCA) and permanent corrective action (PCA) for quality improvement.

jobs.title: Strategic Engagement Lead, USARPAC
jobs.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Team

The Mission Command team is part of the Connected Warfare Division. We build the command and control (C2) tools that help warfighters understand what is happening around them, make faster decisions, and direct their forces. Our work spans the full Lattice portfolio from tactical edge applications to the integrations and data infrastructure that connect them. We spend a lot of our time with the people who actually use these tools: in the field, during exercises, wherever they are.

About the Role

This is not a business development role that happens to live near the customer. The engagement work is the product introduction work. As a Strategic Engagement Lead for USARPAC, you own the path from first contact with a unit or command to a shared understanding of what Lattice and the Connected Warfare portfolio can do for their mission and what it cannot.

Your primary audience is Corps and Division Commanders and their staffs across U.S. Army Pacific. You walk into a room with a two-star or a one-star, often for the first time, and explain what Anduril builds, how it fits into their operational picture, and what preparation looks like before fielding. You translate complex technical capabilities into language that resonates with senior leaders who think in terms of mission, risk, and readiness.

Hawaii is the center of gravity for USARPAC and INDOPACOM’s Army component. The units here train for large-scale combat operations across the Pacific theater, operate in austere and contested environments, and work alongside joint and allied partners daily. You need to understand that context deeply, build trusted relationships within it, and use those relationships to shape how Anduril’s capabilities are understood and adopted.

The profile we are hiring for: someone who can walk into a formation, understand the fight, earn the trust of the people leading it, and credibly connect Anduril’s technology to the problems that keep them up at night. You are not selling—you are advising. You back that up with real curiosity, domain knowledge, and a bias for action.

Key Responsibilities

• Drive NGC2 engagement from the top-down.

• Prepare the battlespace for Army formations receiving NGC2. Validate or redefine Anduril delivery assumptions and ensure customer org structures support NGC2 as a priority.

• Cultivate senior leader advocacy and institutional adoption of NGC2 across Army formations.

• Create and operationalize a repeatable engagement model across Army formations. Evangelize lessons learned from previous customers with new customers early (C2SE for change management, exercise schedule, etc).

• Develop mid-term (6-month) NGC2 product roadmap based on operational leadership priorities. Identify priority applications, features, and integrations and populate product roadmap ahead of fielding.

• Identify efficiencies and opportunities in NGC2 product integration across software, transport, and compute layers based on identified Warfighting needs.

• Evangelize 1P Anduril products within Army formations. Cultivate customer champions for Anduril products.

• Step in as senior Anduril leader for escalation or deescalation when executive leadership engagement is required.

What You’ll Do

• Own the introduction to senior leaders. Conduct initial engagements with Corps and Division Commanders and their staffs across USARPAC, explaining what Lattice and the Connected Warfare portfolio are, what they do, what they don’t do, and what it takes to get ready for fielding.

• Build trusted relationships across USARPAC. Earn the trust of commanders, chiefs of staff, G3/G6 staffs, and subject matter experts. Become a partner who understands how the unit actually fights and operates in the Pacific theater—not just what shows up in a requirements document.

• Know the operational environment. Develop deep familiarity with USARPAC’s mission set, the INDOPACOM theater, and how Army forces organize, train, and operate across the Pacific. Understand the unique challenges of distributed operations, contested logistics, and multi-domain integration in this AOR.

• Translate technology into operational language. Turn complex product capabilities—across applications, data models, integrations, and infrastructure—into clear narratives that connect to how a commander thinks about mission command, fires, maneuver, and sustainment.

• Shape the path to fielding. Advise units on what preparation looks like before they receive Anduril capabilities: network readiness, training requirements, integration with existing systems, and realistic expectations for what the technology will and won’t change on day one.

• Coordinate across Anduril. Pull together product, engineering, field service, and business development teams around a coherent engagement plan. Ensure what we say in the room matches what we can deliver, and feed what you learn back into the product organization.

• Brief well and tell the story. Communicate clearly to a few staff officers, a full command brief, or a GO-level one-on-one. Adjust the level of detail for the audience without losing the substance. Your materials should be authoritative, concise, and operationally relevant.

• Run the room. Lead workshops, working groups, and planning sessions. Get useful information out of a room full of senior leaders, settle competing views, and leave with decisions and next steps.

• Stay connected through fielding. Maintain relationships with units as they move from introduction through fielding and operational use. Track whether the story you told in the first meeting holds up under real conditions, and feed lessons learned back to the team.

• Spot patterns and scale what works. Identify engagement approaches, materials, and narratives that work and package them so the broader team can use them. Don’t reinvent the wheel for every unit.

Who You Are

Anduril moves fast and is scaling fast. We value ambition, hard work, a high bar, and a willingness to disrupt how things are normally done. The people who do well here tend to show these traits:

• Bias for Action. You ask for forgiveness, not permission, and you hate waiting around to be told what to do.

• Outcome-Oriented. You figure out what the mission needs and work backward from there.

• Customer Focused. You have real empathy for the warfighter and you build trust by solving their problems, not pitching products.

• Dive Deep. You sweat the details and get into the weeds to understand the operational problem before proposing a solution.

• You care about the outcomes your engagements produce and hold yourself accountable for follow-through.

• You change direction without drama when the priorities change.

• First Principles Thinking. You solve problems based on what is actually best here, not because a vendor recommended it or because it is how your last company did it.

Required Qualifications

• Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance (TS/SCI preferred).

• 5+ years of experience in strategic engagement, defense consulting, product management, or military operations at the battalion level or above.

• A track record of briefing and building relationships with senior military leaders (COL/GO level).

• Ability to translate complex technical capabilities into operationally relevant narratives, CONOPS, mission threads, and engagement materials.

• Strong understanding of Army operations, staff processes, and doctrine—particularly at the division and corps echelon.

• Experience synthesizing information from multiple sources (product teams, engineers, field users) into a coherent story for a non-technical audience.

• Excellent facilitation skills, including leading interactive planning sessions and working groups with senior participants.

• Strong organizational skills, reliability, and the ability to manage multiple concurrent engagements.

• Willingness to be based in Hawaii with travel up to 30% across the USARPAC footprint and CONUS.

Preferred Qualifications

• Military experience as a commissioned officer or senior NCO, particularly in maneuver, fires, or mission command roles.

• Prior assignment or engagement with USARPAC, 25th Infantry Division, or other Pacific-based Army units.

• Familiarity with INDOPACOM’s operational environment, theater campaign plans, and the unique challenges of the Pacific AOR.

• Experience with command and control systems, mission command philosophy, or military software adoption.

• Working knowledge of data models, system integrations, networking, or distributed and edge systems—enough to reason about what the technology does under the hood.

• A self-starter who does well with ambiguity and loose organizational structure.

• Experience with defense technology fielding or capability introduction at the unit level.

$167,000—$240,000 USD

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. An overview of this role

As a Customer Success Architect, you’ll be a strategic advisor to some of GitLab’s most important customers, helping them connect our DevSecOps platform to their business goals and realize meaningful, long-term outcomes. You’ll partner closely with customers after the sale to turn pre-sales command plans into concrete success plans, guide them along the customer journey, and drive hands-on enablement, adoption, utilization, and maturity. Reporting into a Senior Manager within our North America Customer Success organization, you’ll own a book of customers, act as their primary GitLab liaison for questions and escalations, and coordinate with Product Management, Engineering, Sales, Professional Services, and Support so customers can navigate complex technical and organizational challenges with confidence.

You’ll use your understanding of Git, software development lifecycles, and continuous integration, continuous deployment, and DevSecOps practices to help customers adopt best practices and stay current with new GitLab capabilities. In your first year, success looks like building strong, consultative relationships with key stakeholders, increasing adoption of the GitLab platform, and strengthening retention, growth, and customer satisfaction across your portfolio.

• Provide hands-on technical enablement and onboarding, including education on new GitLab features, releases, and relevant use cases.

• Program manage account escalations, ensuring root causes are understood, follow-up actions are owned, and stakeholders are informed.

• Collaborate with Services and other internal teams to identify and recommend training, enablement, and maturity opportunities aligned to customer needs.

• Practical understanding of Git, common branching strategies, and modern software development lifecycles.

• Working knowledge of continuous integration, continuous deployment, and DevSecOps practices.

• Experience partnering with customers to define business outcomes and translate them into actionable success plans, key goals, and measures.

About Us:

BlackSky is a real-time intelligence company. We own and operate the world's most advanced space-based intelligence platform and provide customers satellite imagery, automated analytics and high-frequency monitoring of strategic locations, economic assets, and events from around the globe. BlackSky is trusted by the most demanding allied military and intelligence organizations and commercial companies to deliver foresight into critical matters that affect national security and the economy. BlackSky's data enables governments and businesses to see, understand and anticipate change as it happens, giving them the ultimate strategic advantage so they can act quickly. Our global team works with cutting-edge technology to make a difference around the world and prides itself on being people-first, customer-focused and fun.

BlackSky is seeking a Principal Hardware Systems Engineer to serve as the primary technical authority for the development of next-generation spaceborne compute platforms supporting advanced Earth observation and real-time onboard processing missions.

This engineer will lead the technical execution of a cutting-edge high-performance computing system deployed in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), featuring high-performance FPGAs and embedded processors, multi-gigabit networking, PCIe, high-speed memory, mass storage, and tightly integrated embedded software.

The successful candidate will own the technical lifecycle of the product from architecture and requirements definition through design implementation, verification, qualification, production transition, and on-orbit deployment. The role requires deep expertise in high-speed digital electronics combined with the ability to lead multidisciplinary teams across hardware, FPGA, embedded software, systems engineering, manufacturing, and mission operations.

As the principal technical authority for the subsystem, you will make critical architectural decisions, drive technical trade studies, manage performance and technical risk, establish verification approaches, and ensure successful delivery of mission-critical flight hardware.

This position reports to the Director, Electrical Engineering and is a hybrid role based out of our Tukwila, WA office.

Responsibilities:

• Serve as the technical authority for a high-performance spaceborne compute platform throughout the entire product lifecycle.

• Develop system and subsystem architectures supporting onboard compute, networking, storage, and mission-processing requirements.

• Lead system trade studies involving processing architectures, FPGA technologies, networking protocols, memory architectures, and storage solutions.

• Own requirements development, decomposition, allocation, and traceability from mission objectives through hardware implementation.

• Define interface requirements between hardware, FPGA firmware, embedded software, payload systems, and spacecraft subsystems.

• Ensure requirements compliance throughout design, verification, qualification, and production.

• Lead technical reviews including SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR, and qualification reviews.

• Support anomaly investigations through root-cause analysis and corrective action implementation.

• Define hardware architecture utilizing technologies including: AMD Adaptive SoCs, embedded processors, 10GbE and 25GbE networking, PCIe Gen4/Gen5 architectures, DDR4/DDR5 memory interfaces, NVMe and solid-state storage, and high-speed serial transceivers

• Guide high-speed digital design activities, including schematic capture, FPGA integration, signal integrity, power integrity, thermal management, and PCB layout.

• Establish design rules and best practices for multi-gigabit high-density digital electronics.

• Review and approve component selections, critical schematics, stackups, routing constraints, and design documentation.

• Establish technology roadmaps and guide strategic technical decisions for future avionics platforms.

• Troubleshoot performance during hardware testing/bring-up

• Interface with external suppliers to develop specifications, exchange data and deliverables, troubleshoot issues, and develop integration and test approaches.

• Participate in Research & Development initiatives and provide support for the establishment of new avionics products

Required Qualifications:

• Bachelor of Science in Electrical or Computer Engineering, or related field involving training in digital electronics design

• 12+ years of experience developing complex digital electronics systems from requirements definition through production deployment, including architecture, implementation, integration, verification, and sustainment in aerospace, defense, or other high-reliability environments.

• Demonstrated technical leadership of multidisciplinary engineering teams including hardware, FPGA, embedded software, systems engineering, and manufacturing.

• Demonstrated ownership of requirements development, decomposition, verification, and compliance closure for complex electronics products.

• Demonstrated ownership of a complex electronics product from architecture definition through verification, qualification, and production release.

• Experience with embedded processors in a SoC FPGA and the programmable logic-processor interfaces associated with those

• Extensive experience designing high reliability applications such as medical and aerospace

• Experience in component selection for devices such as FPGAs, ADCs, DDR, NVRAM, and high speed transceivers (LVDS, Ethernet PHYs, etc)

• Experience designing and bringing up systems utilizing high-speed interfaces such as 10GbE, 25GbE, PCIe Gen3/4/5, DDR4/DDR5, NVMe, JESD204, or other multi-gigabit serial protocols.

• Experience architecting high-performance embedded compute systems utilizing FPGA/SoC devices, multi-gigabit serial interfaces, memory subsystems, and high-speed networking.

• Hands on lab experience using multi-meters, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, programmable power supplies, etc.

• Experience with implementing, prototyping, and bringing up high speed interfaces

• Excellent interpersonal skills and belief in a strong collaborative approach within a multi-disciplinary team

• Must be a U.S. Person

Preferred Qualifications:

• Delivery of multiple products including full ownership from initial concept and architecture definition all the way through production and final implementation

• Master's degree or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or related discipline.

• Experience designing electronics for use in a space environment

• Experience with AMD Versal, Xilinx UltraScale+, Microchip PolarFire, or equivalent FPGA/SoC technologies.

• Experience developing high-performance embedded computing (HPEC) or edge-computing systems.

• Experience with AI/ML acceleration architectures deployed at the edge.

• Experience with Cameralink-High Speed

• Experience defining or designing automated test equipment

• Proficiency with C and Python

Life at BlackSky for full-time benefits eligible employees includes:

• Medical, dental, vision, disability, group term life and AD&D, voluntary life and AD&D insurance

• BlackSky pays 100% of employee-only premiums for medical, dental and vision and contributes $100/month for out-of-pocket expenses!

• 15 days of PTO, 11 Company holidays, four Floating Holidays (pro-rated based on hire date), one day of paid volunteerism leave per year, parental leave and more

• 401(k) pre-tax and Roth deferral options with employer match

• Flexible Spending Accounts

• Employee Stock Purchase Program

• Employee Assistance and Travel Assistance Programs

• Employer matching donations

• Professional development

• Awesome swag

The anticipated salary range for candidates in the Great Seattle Area, WA is 180,000 -200,000 per year. The final compensation package offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on specific background and education. BlackSky is a multi-state employer, and this pay scale may not reflect salary ranges in other states or locations outside of the Great Seattle Area.

BlackSky is committed to hiring and retaining a diverse workforce. We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity. All Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law.

To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.

jobs.title: Floater - Macon
jobs.description:
Who Are We?

AppleTree Prep is an established, state licensed center that is committed to investing in our staff and developing a caring, friendly community of educators and learners. We have attained a 3-star quality rating through the Quality Rated program. It is our mission to grow independent and confident, compassionate individuals. Our dedication to creating a stimulating and enriching environment for students and teachers alike makes us an amazing place to work!

Appletree Prep Macon– Floater

Where you play a key role in shaping a child’s earliest learning experiences.

WHO WE ARE

Appletree Prep Macon is part of a growing network of early childhood education schools committed to creating safe, engaging, and inspiring environments where children thrive.

We believe early childhood education is where everything begins – first steps, first friendships, and the foundation for a lifetime of learning. Our classrooms are communities where curiosity is encouraged, creativity is nurtured, and every child is valued.

WHY JOIN US

Our people are at the heart of everything we do. When you join our team, you become part of a collaborative, supportive environment where your work helps create a positive experience for children and families each day.

As a Floater Teacher, you’ll gain hands-on classroom experience and build the skills to grow your career in early childhood education.

ABOUT THE ROLE

In this role, you’ll support the classroom team in creating a safe, engaging environment where children can learn and grow. You’ll assist with daily activities, provide active supervision, and help bring the curriculum to life while ensuring a smooth, positive classroom experience.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

• Help create a safe, nurturing, and engaging classroom environment for all children

• Support daily activities and curriculum implementation alongside the lead teacher

• Always provide active supervision, ensuring safety and compliance with required ratios

• Support children’s development through positive guidance, interaction, and play

• Assist with classroom routines, organization, and communication with families, while supporting overall school operations

Each day is an opportunity to make a positive impact on a child’s growth and early learning experience.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

We’re seeking dependable, positive individuals who enjoy working with children and contributing to a supportive team environment.

You’ll be a great fit if you:

• Have a passion for working with young children

• Bring a positive, patient, and supportive approach

• Are dependable and show up ready to contribute each day

• Work well as part of a collaborative team

• Are open to learning, feedback, and growth

• Adapt well in a fast-paced classroom environment

Qualifications:

• High school diploma or equivalent (GED) required. Coursework or degree in Early Childhood Education or related field preferred.

• Previous experience working with young children in a childcare, preschool, or similar setting preferred.

• Basic understanding of classroom procedures and willingness to learn state licensing and compliance requirements.

• Must meet all state-specific education, certification (including CPR/First Aid, where required), licensing, and regulatory requirements, including the ability to pass a background check and complete ongoing professional development.

• Effective communication skills and a collaborative approach to working with children, families, and team members.

• Must be at least 18 years of age.

• Ability to work Monday-Friday 2PM-6:30PM

WHAT YOU’LL GET

• Competitive pay ($15-$16 hourly based on experience and location)

• Paid time off (PTO) and holiday pay

• Discounted childcare

• Medical, dental, and vision benefits

• Option to purchase various voluntary insurance plans

• 401(k) options

• Ongoing leadership development and career growth opportunities

jobs.title: Director, Professional Services Technical Architects
jobs.description:
GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As the Director, Technical Architects on GitLab's AMER Professional Services team, you oversee one of the most technically credible and customer-facing groups in the organization. This team helps turn customer priorities into real adoption and measurable outcomes by guiding complex implementations, shaping new service patterns, and bringing emerging GitLab capabilities into production environments.

You'll own the Global Technical Architecture practice across both presales and delivery, managing a team of AMER Technical Architects who work on complex customer needs, early-stage offerings, and strategic engagements. This role is well suited for someone who can coach senior technical talent, bring structure to ambiguity, and keep the team focused on customer outcomes instead of task completion.

In your first year, you'll focus on stabilizing and growing the team, tightening the link between presales scoping and delivery, and turning field work into repeatable offerings. You'll work alongside architects in areas including AI, security, and broader platform architecture, while helping the team turn what they learn in the field into repeatable methods that can scale across Professional Services.

Some examples of our projects:

• Running technical discovery, scoping, and delivery for complex Professional Services engagements in AMER

• Turning early customer work on new GitLab capabilities into repeatable delivery kits, standards, and service patterns

What you’ll do

• Hire, manage, and develop a growing AMER Technical Architecture team, including Intermediate, Senior, and Staff Technical Architects working across platform, AI, and security-related customer engagements.

• Lead the global Technical Architecture practice, aligning architects in AMER, EMEA, and APJ on shared standards for scoping, statement of work review, service offerings and delivery leadership.

• Manage the practice end to end, covering presales collaboration, engagement scoping, technical delivery oversight, staffing, utilization, and forecast alignment, with accountability for improving utilization, delivery quality, and forecast accuracy.

• Coach architects to grow from hands-on implementers into technical leaders and credible advisors on most of their engagements, with a focus on customer outcomes, strong technical judgment, and consultative communication.

• Partner on complex presales motions with Engagement Managers on estimation, solution framing, technical objection handling, statement of work assumptions, and technical risk to build customer confidence, improve scoping accuracy, and strengthen delivery readiness.

• Join strategic customer conversations where senior technical expertise helps build credibility, clarify ambiguity, and improve the path to successful delivery.

• Guide the team through first-mover delivery of new GitLab capabilities, helping shape how emerging offerings are tested, delivered, and improved in real customer environments to shorten time to production and increase successful adoption.

• Turn lessons from strategic engagements into reusable templates, architecture guidance, migration patterns, and implementation standards that increase reuse and improve delivery consistency across the broader Professional Services organization.

• Represent the Technical Architecture practice in AMER Professional Services management discussions and partner with adjacent functions to improve coordination, service evolution, and delivery consistency.

What you’ll bring

• Proven experience managing senior technical professionals in a services, consulting, or Professional Services environment, with a strong track record of coaching, performance management, and career development.

• Working knowledge of GitLab, software development, site reliability and infrastructure engineering, security, cloud architecture, and agile delivery, with enough depth to guide technical direction and build credibility with highly experienced architects.

• Experience running consultative engagements by linking technical work to business goals and keeping teams focused on customer value and realized outcomes.

• Experience with technically complex presales work, including discovery, scoping, estimation, solution definition, and risk assessment.

• Experience running a billable team against utilization targets, with a clear grasp of how utilization, margin, and forecast accuracy drive Professional Services revenue.

• Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in fast-moving environments where offerings, priorities, and organizational needs continue to evolve.

• Experience building or improving repeatable delivery methods such as playbooks, standards, service kits, architecture patterns, or implementation guidance.

• A servant-leadership style built on empathy and continuous improvement: you remove blockers for your team, act on what retrospectives surface, and build processes that make it easy to do the right thing.

• Experience leading customer conversations at every level, from platform engineers to the CTO, giving clear feedback, and aligning cross-functional stakeholders around delivery direction.

• Familiarity with GitLab-relevant domains such as AI-powered developer workflows, security, DevSecOps, or enterprise platform adoption is helpful, along with experience ramping up quickly in adjacent areas where needed.

• Experience using AI to scale how your team scopes, documents, and delivers work.

• Ability to travel up to 25%.

About the team

The Professional Services team helps customers adopt GitLab in ways that create lasting value. Within that organization, the Technical Architecture team handles some of the most complex and ambiguous work. This includes shaping early delivery approaches for new capabilities, contributing to high-impact customer engagements, and creating the patterns that help the wider organization scale successful services.

You'll manage a growing AMER team of Technical Architects, lead the global Technical Architecture practice, and work closely with Engagement Management, Professional Services Operations, Customer Experience Engineering, and other Professional Services colleagues. We play an important role in setting the technical standard for delivery while also helping define how new services should be scoped, delivered, and improved over time.

GitLab works in an all-remote, asynchronous environment built on transparency, iteration, collaboration, and empowered ownership. In our team, that means giving managers and architects the latitude to solve hard problems, exchange what they learn openly, and continuously improve how the practice runs. If you enjoy developing strong technical talent, creating clarity in fast-changing environments, and helping customers succeed through thoughtful consulting, you'll have a meaningful place to make an impact with us.

The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. See more information on our benefits and equity. Sales roles are also eligible for incentive pay targeted at up to 100% of the offered base salary.

United States Salary Range

$207,400—$348,840 USD

How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees

• Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being

• Flexible Paid Time Off

• Team Member Resource Groups

• Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan

• Growth and Development Fund

• Parental Leave

Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from underrepresented groups are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.

Country Hiring Guidelines: GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.

GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. See also GitLab’s EEO Policy and EEO is the Law. jobs.description:
Bethesda Brings out the Best in Talented, Caring People!

At Bethesda, more than 1,200 employees dedicate their careers to improving the lives of others.

As a team member at Bethesda, you'll enjoy great benefits such as: 403b, daily pay, bonuses, career advancement opportunities, and holiday pay.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Who we are:

Formic is on a mission to reshape American manufacturing by making automation accessible to every factory. As labor constraints rise, costs increase, and global competition intensifies, automation is no longer optional for manufacturers that want to stay competitive.

We deliver automation through a Robotics-as-a-Service model that combines industrial robotics, proprietary software, and full-service support into a single, integrated solution. By removing the traditional barriers of cost, complexity, and risk, we enable manufacturers to deploy automation quickly and realize measurable gains in throughput, safety, and operational efficiency without large upfront capital investment.

Backed by leading investors including Lux Capital, Initialized Capital, Blackhorn Ventures, and Mitsubishi HC Capital North America, Formic is scaling rapidly and building the foundation for a new era of high-performance, Made in America production.

About the team:

Formic's Business Systems team builds and manages the software, data infrastructure, and integrations that power our operations.

Our work touches nearly every part of the company. We build internal applications that help teams manage robot deployments and field service, connect operational data across platforms, and develop AI-powered tools that make information more accessible and work more efficient. We also help shape the systems behind our sales, marketing, finance, and other business processes.

Some solutions are custom-built applications. Others involve integrating existing platforms, automating workflows, or rethinking how information moves through the business. We work directly with the people using these systems and own what we deliver, including adoption, reliability, and ongoing improvement.

We're a small team with significant autonomy, tackling technical challenges across a robotics company where the software we build has a direct impact on real-world operations.

About the role:

We're looking for a technically strong, AI-forward builder who can turn complex business problems into working software.

You'll work directly with teams across Formic to identify opportunities and build solutions, whether that's developing an internal application, connecting systems that don't communicate, automating an operational process, or applying AI to make existing tools more useful.

You'll have the autonomy to determine what to build and how to build it, along with responsibility for getting it into production and making sure it works. We want someone who moves quickly, makes sound technical decisions, and cares as much about adoption and reliability as development.

This isn't a traditional product management role or one focused exclusively on AI. It's a hands-on opportunity for someone who loves building software and wants to see the impact of their work.

We care more about what you've built than your job title or career path. You might come from software engineering, applied AI, technical product development, business systems engineering, or a startup where you've worn several hats. What matters is that you know how to turn ideas into working software and can show us what you've shipped.

In this role you will:

• Build and maintain internal applications, AI-powered tools, automations, and integrations that solve problems across Formic

• Work directly with employees and business leaders to understand existing processes, uncover inefficiencies, and determine what should be built

• Design technical solutions, including application architecture, APIs, databases, data pipelines, and integrations with existing platforms

• Experiment with LLMs, AI agents, and emerging development tools, applying them where they offer a meaningful advantage

• Connect information across business systems to improve data quality, visibility, and decision-making

• Take projects from initial discovery through prototyping, development, deployment, and ongoing support

• Build with security, reliability, maintainability, and scalability in mind, including appropriate testing and monitoring

• Gather feedback, measure adoption and results, and continuously improve the products you deliver

• Collaborate with engineering and other technical teams when projects require shared infrastructure or specialized expertise

• Help determine the priorities, architecture, and technical direction of our Business Systems function

What makes you a great fit:

• A strong track record of personally building and shipping software, internal products, automations, or other technical solutions that people rely on

• Solid software development skills, including experience working with APIs, databases, and modern application development tools

• Proficiency in at least one modern programming language, such as Python or TypeScript, and experience working with APIs, databases, and SQL

• Hands-on experience integrating systems and working with data across multiple platforms

• Practical experience using AI in software development or building AI-powered applications, with genuine curiosity about emerging capabilities

• The ability to make thoughtful technical decisions without overengineering solutions

• Strong product instincts. You can understand what users need, distinguish symptoms from underlying problems, and prioritize work based on impact

• Comfort working independently, navigating ambiguity, and owning projects from beginning to end

• An appreciation for what happens after launch, including testing, documentation, monitoring, maintenance, and user adoption

• The ability to communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical colleagues

• A bias toward action, intellectual curiosity, and genuine interest in how businesses operate

Bonus points if you have:

• Experience building with LLM APIs, AI agents, retrieval-augmented generation, or agentic workflows

• Experience building and deploying cloud-based applications

• Familiarity with CRM, ERP, finance, or operational systems and the data that connects them

• Experience with workflow orchestration, event-driven integrations, or data engineering

• Experience building applications that handle sensitive business information

• A background in robotics, manufacturing, industrial automation, logistics, or field service operations.

• Experience working in a startup or small technical team where you've had substantial ownership.

Our Total Rewards:

At Formic, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported both professionally and personally. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits and perks package for full-time, U.S.-based team members, including:

• Equity in Formic: Participate in our stock option program and share in the success of a fast-growing start-up backed by leading global investors

• Competitive & Uncapped Commission Structure: Designed to reward performance and impact in commission-eligible roles

• Comprehensive Healthcare Coverage: Medical, dental, and vision insurance through Blue Cross Blue Shield and Unum, with 99% of employee premiums covered and 75% coverage for dependents, with optional buy-up plans available

• Additional Insurance Benefits: FSA and DCFSA, life insurance, short-term disability, and long-term disability through Unum, all 100% employer-paid

• Employee Assistance Program (EAP): Fully funded by Formic, offering support when you need it most

• Paid Parental Leave Program: Up to 12 weeks of paid parental leave

• Company-sponsored 401(k): Invest in your future with our company-facilitated retirement savings plan

• Home Office Stipend: A one-time allowance for fully remote and hybrid employees to support an at-home or on-the-road work setup

• Monthly Cell Phone Reimbursement: Monthly stipend toward personal phone and internet expenses

• Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need, when you need it, supported by our flexible PTO policy

Compensation Philosophy

Formic’s pay and equity packages are thoughtfully benchmarked against peer companies at a similar growth stage. Equity represents a meaningful part of our mutual investment: when Formic succeeds, so do you.

Final offers are customized based on experience, geographic location, market considerations, and a candidate’s preferred balance of cash and equity. Our goal is to attract and reward top talent who will have significant impact, and we are open to thoughtful discussions to align on the right structure.

Compensation Range:

$135,000—$175,000 USD

What we look for:

We’re building this company from the ground up, and every person we hire has an outsized impact on our culture, performance, and trajectory. While each team member brings unique strengths and perspectives, we look for people who align with our Operating Principles and embody them in action. If this sounds like you, Formic may be the right place for you!

• Fearless Optimism: You make bold bets and default optimistic. You believe in the mission, aren’t paralyzed by risk, and fear inaction more than failure. You see ambiguity as opportunity and bring energy to building what doesn’t yet exist.

• Create the Magic: You absorb complexity so customers don’t have to. Whether your customer is external or internal, you focus on delivering experiences that are clear, fast, value-added, and outcome-driven. You don’t say “not my job.” You make things work.

• Today, Not Tomorrow: You have a bias to action. You close the loop. You take extreme ownership. You understand that speed compounds, and you don’t confuse activity with results.

• Seek Truth: You think from first principles. You value data over ego and strong opinions loosely held. You’re willing to challenge assumptions, including your own, in pursuit of the best answer.

• Made of Rubber: You are resolute and adaptable. When things break or priorities shift, you rebound stronger. You treat setbacks as learning moments and move forward with grit.

• One Formic: You operate without silos. You practice radical helpfulness, document clearly, and make clean handoffs. You assume positive intent and prioritize team success over individual credit.

Equal Opportunity Employment:

Formic is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion or religious creed, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, marital status, family or parental status, disability, military or veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. All employment decisions are based on a person’s merit, business needs, and role requirements. If you require further accommodations or have questions regarding accessibility of our roles, please reach out to accessibility@formic.co.

AI Use:

At Formic, fairness and transparency are at the heart of our hiring process. We use AI-powered tools in some interviews to help our teams evaluate candidate responses, but all final hiring decisions are made by humans. You can learn more about how AI is used in our recruitment process by reviewing our AI Hiring Disclosure linked here.

jobs.description:
At Podium, we build an AI Workforce that helps local businesses turn every conversation into revenue. More than 60,000 businesses across Auto, Home Services, and Aesthetics trust Podium to drive growth 24/7, from capturing new leads to re-engaging past customers.

Two and a half years ago, we made a deliberate shift from building software for local businesses to building AI Employees that work for them. We’ve crossed $150M in AI ARR, deployed more than 20,000 AI Employees, and helped customers generate over $13B in revenue.

Inc. Magazine named Podium the Best AI Implementation, OpenAI highlighted us for building AI Agents that drive revenue, and G2 ranked us the #1 AI Agent for Business Operations.

Podium is AI-native in every sense. We build AI for our customers, we build AI tools for ourselves, and we use AI in every role across the company.

We hire exceptional people, hold them to high standards, and give them room to make an impact. We look for people who are all-in on AI and eager to stay on the cutting edge, both in what we build for customers and in how they operate day to day. If you’re hungry for growth, aligned with our operating principles, and ready to get to work, you won’t find a better place to accelerate your career.

About this opportunity

As the Interim Vertical Marketing Manager for MedSpa, you'll own demand generation campaigns, with a primary focus on trade shows, field events, and partner marketing, that put Podium in front of medspa owners and turn interest into revenue. You'll become the expert on the medspa customer: their business challenges, buying behavior, seasonal dynamics, and competitive landscape. This role sits at the intersection of strategy and execution. You'll set the plan for your channels and roll up your sleeves to bring it to life. You'll work cross-functionally with Sales, Product, and Customer Success to build campaigns that fit the needs of medspa businesses and drive efficient growth. The ideal candidate is a full-stack marketer who thinks in systems, moves with urgency, and makes sharp decisions with imperfect information. You're a heavy AI user who builds workflows to move faster. You love having a bookings target, and you know how to build a playbook, not just inherit one.

What you will be doing

Own the roadmap, track pacing against goals, and keep iterating to maximize new customer growth in the medspa space.

• Drive demand generation campaigns: Plan and execute targeted campaigns that engage medspa owners, build pipeline, and turn interest into sales opportunities.

• Drive our partner marketing activities: Partner marketing is a core vertical channel for Podium. Develop the strategy and run campaigns with high-leverage partners to convert their audiences into paying customers. You'll also tap the partner network to build a pipeline of influencers who become Podium evangelists.

• Own trade shows and field events: Run Podium's in-person presence, from pre-show targeting to on-site execution to follow-up. You'll own and execute our biggest trade show of the year, the Medical Spa Show, and run field events through both partner-led events and intimate, Podium-hosted gatherings for around 20 medspa owners, prospects, and customers.

• Put AI to work: Use AI to plan, create, and analyze faster, and build workflows that make your channels more efficient.

• Understand the customer: Identify their pain points, learn how their businesses run, and figure out the best channels and language to reach them. Share what you learn across marketing and the broader org.

• Collaborate cross-functionally: Partner with Sales, Product, and Support to align vertical efforts and build campaigns that resonate with prospects and customers.

What you should have

• 5-8 years of experience in marketing, demand generation, or similar, preferably in B2B SaaS

• Hands-on experience across channels like events, partner or field marketing, and third-party media, influencer, and affiliate

• Strong understanding of funnel metrics, along with campaign planning, strategy, and campaign execution

• Exceptional bias to action and the drive to build and execute with minimal hand-holding

• Analytical and ROI-minded, comfortable digging into performance data to find insights and drive decisions

• Heavy AI user who builds workflows and can show what you've made

• Customer-centric mindset, with the ability to empathize with customers and put their needs first

• Collaborative mindset and the ability to adapt across teams

Nice-to-haves

• Experience marketing to SMBs or local businesses, or marketing an AI product

• Familiarity with the aesthetics industry and how medspas buy

• Willingness to work in office at our Lehi office 5 days/week (Minimum requirement: 3 days/week)

Why you'll love working here

• Join the leaders in AI agents

• Unlock career-defining growth

• Build with world-class talent

• Make a real impact on local business

Contract details

• 35-40 hours/week

• Overlap and shadowing time with the outgoing Vertical Marketing Manager before her leave begins, plus a structured handoff at the end of the engagement

jobs.title: Legal, Commercial
jobs.description:
ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.



THE ROLE

We're hiring a senior attorney to partner with our GTM team on enterprise deals as Baseten moves upmarket. You'll work with Sales, Security, Finance, Marketing, Eng and Product on our largest and most complex customer deals across large enterprise, regulated industries and AI-native companies.

At Baseten, commercial and product are the same thing. What we sell is inference: compute, orchestration, deployment, and optimization delivered as the production backbone for our customers' products. Closing a deal here means understanding how our product works (model deployment, data flows, multi-cloud routing, and latency and throughput) and the novel legal issues it raises. This is a role for a commercially minded product lawyer who wants to sit at that intersection.

You'll own enterprise contracting end to end, with a focus on our largest and most regulated customers, where legal is a key partner in the deal. Like everyone on this team, you'll also flex onto other work where you're needed.



RESPONSIBILITIES 
Own the full lifecycle of enterprise agreements (MSAs, Order Forms, DPAs, BAAs, SLAs, security addenda, financial services addenda, NDAs) as a strong, trusted partner to Sales and GTM throughout the deal cycle

 - Independently lead negotiations on our largest and most complex deals, and engage directly with customer counsel, procurement, and executive stakeholders

 - Help GTM understand how our products map to legal terms, and explain complex concepts in plain language for customers, Sales and other internal teams

 - Own Baseten's positions for regulated customers in healthcare, life sciences, and financial services, partnering with Security, GRC, and AI, Privacy & Governance on operational-resilience, data-protection, and upstream commitments

 - Structure non-standard deals with Finance and RevOps, and help build the legal framework for GTM channels and distribution models

 - Build templates, playbooks, and enablement for Legal, Sales, and supporting teams, and drive the processes that help us scale

 - Partner with Sales on deal strategy and drive deal velocity: know which terms to hold, which to trade, and how to explain the difference to an AE, a customer's GC, or Baseten’s CLO

 - Stay current on AI legal and regulatory developments, and recommend changes to our positions as the product, market, and law evolve

 - Mentor others and help us scale the team; may assist on partnerships, M&A, and other strategic or one-off transactions

REQUIREMENTS

 - JD and active bar membership in good standing

 - 8+ years of commercial / technology transactions experience, including in-house experience at an AI-native, B2B SaaS, cloud, or developer-infrastructure company

 - Track record negotiating complex agreements with large enterprises and regulated customers across healthcare, life sciences, financial services, retail and digital, and AI-native companies

 - Working knowledge of regimes common in regulated deals (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA, DORA and security and audit commitments), and comfort discussing them directly with customers

 - Comfort working with technical products and translating how they work into clear legal positions
